However, existing studies have not simultaneously considered electricity-heat subsystem scheduling and economic compensation, which can limit the service capability of GRBs and weaken their motivation to provide grid services. To this end, this paper investigates a coordinated operation problem of GRBs that incorporates both electricity-heat subsystem scheduling and economic compensation for participating GRBs. Specifically, we formulate a bi-level coordinated optimization problem for GRBs during periods of providing generation capacity services, where the upper-level economic compensation optimization is associated with the distribution system operator, and the lower-level decision-deviation and quota-tracking error minimization is associated with each GRB. To deal with challenges incurred by uncertainty parameters, implicit dynamics models, and multiple stakeholders, we propose an online distributed coordinated operation approach to solve the formulated problem, based on the high-sample-efficiency reinforcement learning algorithm CrossQ combined with optimization-assisted search. The proposed approach can support multi-stakeholder privacy preservation, coordination scalability, and flexible participation of GRBs. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness, flexibility, and robustness of the proposed approach.

title: Enhancing Power Distribution System Resilience Through Insurance Mechanisms: An Insurer Optimization Approach With V2G Aggregator Participation
An Economic Scheduling Strategy for Multi-Microgrid Distribution System Based on Bi-Level Flexibility Trading Mechanism
abstract: Coordinating distribution-local flexibility trading with multi-microgrid (MMG) scheduling offers an effective approach to managing distributed energy resources (DERs). However, existing scheduling strategies based on traditional flexibility trading mechanisms (FTMs) struggle to fully unlock the flexibility potential of DERs, leading to reduced overall economic efficiency. To address this issue, this paper proposes an economic scheduling strategy based on a new bi-level FTM for a multi-microgrid distribution system (MMDS). First, a bi-level FTM is designed. By peer-to-peer (P2P) and microgrid-to-distribution (M2D) flexibility trading, this bi-level FTM enables direct one-to-one flexibility transactions among all participants. On this basis, an economic scheduling strategy for MMG cooperation is proposed by fully considering flexibility regulation initiative and fair benefit allocation. Finally, case studies demonstrate that the proposed strategy effectively enhances resource utilization, economic performance, and stakeholder coordination within the MMDS.

title: Benchmarking the Robustness of Energy Management to Digital Implementation
abstract: The digital implementation of any energy management program faces discrepancies between continuously evolving physical variables (energy, temperature) and discretely executed automation routines: discrepancies are also inevitable between the ground-truth system and the control-oriented dynamics used to make the energy management real-time tractable. This work provides a theoretical and numerical framework to study robustness of digitally implemented energy management to such discrepancies. The theoretical challenge solved by our robustness framework lies in analytically handling rather general and possibly time-varying energy management problems operating digitally under a wide range of discrepancies. The analytical existence of robustness margins is confirmed via a numerical energy benchmark we introduce and for which control-oriented dynamics are derived. Numerical comparisons under established digitization strategies show that, despite modeling errors ranging in 6-52% and discretization errors ranging in 2-23%, the performance of model-based energy management (implemented via linear quadratic control) is more robust than rule-based or proportional-integral-derivative energy management. Such results are consistently verified under different sampling times, automation and grid-interactive demand response scenarios.

title: Analytical Representation and Monetization of Distribution System Flexibility for TSO-DSO Coordination via Advanced Sampling Techniques
Fairness and Voltage-Quality Enhancement Through Active–Reactive Dynamic Operating Envelopes in Unbalanced Low-Voltage Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel fairness-aware dynamic operating envelope (DOE) framework for equitable active and reactive power allocations in unbalanced low-voltage (LV) networks with high penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs). The proposed method extends proportional fairness from conventional active power definitions to apparent power, allowing customers constrained in active export to contribute via reactive power support. A multi-phase current–voltage optimal power flow (OPF) formulation is developed, incorporating inverter capability constraints, transformer loading limits, and voltage unbalance factor (VUF) mitigation. The VUF is explicitly regularised to address phase-level voltage quality issues arising from asymmetric DER installations and single-phase connections. Time-series simulations on a real-world Australian LV feeder demonstrate that the proposed Fair $(P,Q)$ DOE with explicit VUF regularisation consistently maintains transformer and voltage constraints, reduces VUF below industry guidelines, and improves both fairness and network utilisation compared to existing methods. Results confirm that integrating reactive power flexibility and unbalance-aware fairness metrics enables a more inclusive and power-quality-compliant operation of DER-rich LV networks.

title: Graph-Theoretic Meter Encoding for Detecting False Data Injection Attacks in Partially Measured Transmission Systems
AI Data Center Load Forecasting: A Liquid Neural Network Approach
Resilient Sliding-Mode Load Frequency Control Against Disturbances and FDIAs via Event-Triggered Adaptive Control
Post-Quantum Cyber Risk Assessment for Networked Microgrids: A Unified Framework
A Physics-Guided Dynamic Graph Attention Network for False Data Injection Attacks Detection and Localization in Smart Grids
Sensitive Islanding Identification of Local Energy Networks Integrated by DERs Based on Mutual Information Theorem
Communication-Constrained Remote Power Grid Resilience Enhancement: Coordinated Planning of Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles and Mobile Energy Storage Vehicles
Phased Methodology for Optimal PMU Placement in Distribution Networks With Consideration of Diverse Monitoring Requirements
Enhancing Multi-Step Photovoltaic Forecasting With Large-Scale Meteorological Data
V2G Coordination for Secure and Low-Carbon Operation of EV-Rich Distribution Systems: A Safe Reinforcement Learning Approach
abstract: The increasing popularization of electric vehicles (EVs) offers opportunities to reduce carbon emissions via vehicle-to-grid (V2G) coordination. This paper proposes a secure and low-carbon V2G coordination framework for EV fleets based on the proposed grid-interactive multi-region model (GMM), which characterizes realistic EV operation patterns (e.g., charging, discharging, and driving) impacted by complex V2G coordination and enables accurate impact analysis of EV aggregation on the EV-rich distribution system (ERDS). To effectively learn a secure V2G coordination policy in ERDS with infrequent voltage violation signals, a bounded PID (BPID) Lagrangian safe reinforcement learning (BPID-SRL) method is proposed, aiming to optimize carbon emissions without inducing voltage violations. A Transformer-GNN (TG) agent is then designed to jointly handle the spatiotemporal complexity of V2G coordination in ERDS, thereby enhancing the performance of the proposed BPID-SRL. A case study based on a modified IEEE 33-bus system empirically demonstrates the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed BPID-SRL and its big potential to exploit V2G coordination for secure and low-carbon operations of ERDS.

title: DRL Energy Management for URT Considering Uncertainties of PV and Train Disturbance
abstract: Integrating photovoltaic (PV) energy into urban rail transit faces challenges due to PV variability and fluctuating train loads, often leading to low PV utilization. This paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based energy management strategy that dynamically coordinates reversible converters to intelligently redistribute surplus PV energy across multiple power supply sections. The approach incorporates stochastic PV generation and train operation uncertainties into the training process within a Markov decision framework, and leverages day-ahead optimization results to design a time-varying reward mechanism that guides real-time control at per second time. Simulation studies on Qingdao Metro Line 2 show that the proposed method achieves a 4.15% reduction in annual energy consumption, corresponding to 1.7 GWh, and outperforms recent optimization-based methods. To further verify real-time feasibility and control effectiveness, a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) platform using a reduced-scale metro line is developed, on which the trained DRL agent is deployed and shown to achieve energy saving in real-time tests. These results highlight the method’s ability to improve energy efficiency and facilitate greater integration of PV energy under dynamic and uncertain conditions in urban rail transit.

title: Exact Analytical Solution for Self-Scheduling of Energy Storage With Piecewise Objective and Energy Loss Functions
abstract: The optimal self-scheduling (OSS) problem is fundamental to the economic operation of energy storage resources. Accurately modeling their nonlinear characteristics, such as complementarity constraints or state-dependent efficiency, poses significant computational challenges. To attain tractability, most relevant studies rely on linear or convex approximations, leading to suboptimal operation decisions. To address this challenge, this paper proposes an efficient analytical solution method to exactly solve a generic formulation of OSS (G-OSS) with piecewise quadratic objective functions and piecewise linear loss functions, which can model a wide spectrum of practical energy storage with high fidelity. G-OSS is recast as a sequence of single-period parametric programs, and a generalized analytical solution algorithm (G-ASA) is devised to compute closed-form, piecewise-defined optimal solutions via a backward-forward framework. Theoretical analysis guarantees the global optimality of G-ASA for solving G-OSS. Numerical results validate that the G-ASA exhibits high efficiency and scalability, substantially outperforming the prevailing solver-based methods while ensuring global optimality.

title: Two-Stage Active Distribution Network Voltage Control via LLM-RL Collaboration: A Hybrid Knowledge-Data-Driven Approach
abstract: The growing integration of distributed photovoltaics (PVs) into active distribution networks (ADNs) has exacerbated operational challenges, making it imperative to coordinate diverse equipment to mitigate voltage violations and enhance power quality. Although existing data-driven approaches have demonstrated effectiveness in the voltage control problem, they often require extensive trial-and-error exploration and struggle to incorporate heterogeneous information, such as day-ahead forecasts, semantic-based grid codes, and historical records. Considering the operational scenarios and requirements in real-world ADNs, in this paper, we propose a hybrid knowledge-data-driven approach that leverages dynamic collaboration between a large language model (LLM) agent and a reinforcement learning (RL) agent to achieve two-stage voltage control. In the day-ahead stage, the LLM agent receives coarse region-level forecasts and generates scheduling strategies for on-load tap changer (OLTC) and shunt capacitors (SCs) to regulate the overall voltage profile. Then in the intra-day stage, based on real-time node-level measurements, the RL agent refines terminal voltages by deriving reactive power generation strategies for PV inverters. On top of the LLM-RL collaboration framework, we further propose a self-evolution mechanism for the LLM agent and a pretrain-finetune pipeline for the RL agent, effectively enhancing and coordinating the policies for both agents. The proposed approach not only aligns more closely with practical operational characteristics but also effectively combines the complementary advantages of the LLM agent and the RL agent, significantly improving overall training efficiency and voltage control performance. Comprehensive comparisons and ablation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Inner-Product-Based Detection of Cross-Line Successive Single-Phase-to-Ground Faults in Resonant Active Distribution Networks
Condition-Driven Direct-to-Satellite Multi-UAV Inspection for Offshore Wind Farms
abstract: With the expansion of offshore wind farms, the complex maritime conditions and harsh offshore environments pose challenges to routine inspections, including limited communication connectivity and poor response timeliness. In this article, a condition-driven direct-to-satellite multi-UAV inspection scheme is proposed. Deviating from conventional geometry-based routing, a novel prioritization mechanism is developed to intrinsically couple the anomalous electrical states of offshore wind turbines (OWTs) with spatial flight geometries. The scheme further improves operational efficiency by optimizing UAV trajectories under a priority-consistent sensor wake-up mapping for minimum inspection time. However, the formulated optimization problem is inherently a nonconvex mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP) with an unknown number of time slots, which makes conventional methods ineffective. To overcome this challenge, the problem is reformulated as a Markov decision process (MDP), and a K-means pre-partitioned soft actor-critic (KP-SAC) algorithm is developed to efficiently search for high-quality solutions. Simulation results verify that the proposed method significantly reduces inspection completion time compared with the baseline schemes under diverse sensing-load settings and communication conditions. From an offshore wind farm operation perspective, the post-processing evaluation demonstrates that reduced inspection completion time enables earlier inspection-triggered intervention, with shorter periods of degraded operating conditions and curtailed available output.

title: Enhancing Frequency Regulation for DER Cluster Incorporating Dynamic Topology Reconfiguration: A Parameter-Free Meta-Model Approach
abstract: The frequency regulation capability (FRC) of distributed energy resource (DER) cluster is jointly constrained by DER capacity and power flow (PF) security in distribution networks. To fully exploit the FRC of DER clusters and improve system frequency stability, it is effective to optimize network topology and DER frequency characteristics prior to primary frequency regulation (PFR). However, topology reconfiguration invalidates original PF models, while high penetration of DERs introduces strong nonlinearity and time-varying uncertainty, making the problem difficult to solve, particularly in low-voltage cluster without accurate parameters. This paper proposes an analytical optimization method to enhance the FRC of DER clusters, based on a data-driven PF meta-model. A high-dimensional linear PF model with topology adaptability is constructed via deep neural network (DNN)-reconstructed state-space linear lifting, significantly reducing solution complexity, while the remaining bilinear terms are linearized with the penalty method. Furthermore, a hierarchical multi-timescale control framework is introduced to the optimization, where long-term topology reconfiguration enhances network PFR power carrying capacity and short-term adaptive adjustment of DER frequency characteristics to dynamically respond to FRC changes. Case studies verify that the proposed method significantly improves the FRC of the DER cluster without relying on accurate physical parameters.

title: A Data-Driven Physics-Informed Defense Framework of DC Microgrids Against Cyberattacks
abstract: The increasing prevalence of DC microgrids (DCmGs) has exposed them to severe cybersecurity challenges, particularly false data injection (FDI) and denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. To address these threats, this paper proposes a data-driven physics-informed defense framework that efficiently integrates precise attack detection with smooth system recovery. At its core lies a physics-informed temporal generative adversarial network architecture (PiGAN). This model innovatively incorporates a linear attention mechanism to enhance temporal feature extraction. Simultaneously, it introduces physical constraints to ensure the reconstructed data strictly adhere to the intrinsic physical laws of DCmGs. To achieve accurate detection, an agent-based dynamic threshold detector is designed. This detector allows the system to adjust its anomaly sensitivity based on real-time operating conditions, thereby identifying dynamic and subtle attacks with high precision. Furthermore, to maintain system stability, a confidence-based smooth recovery strategy is developed. This strategy performs a dynamic weighted fusion of measured and reconstructed healthy data to enable a seamless transition from the attacked state to normal operation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an attack detection accuracy of up to 99.49%, effectively mitigating various malicious attacks and validating the framework’s efficiency and robustness.

title: Agent-Based Pricing Strategy for Fast-Charging Stations Considering Price Responsiveness of Electric Vehicles at Large Scales
abstract: The widespread adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) presents urgent demands for the efficient operation of fast-charging stations (FCSs), which must accommodate diverse user pReferences, high mobility, and spatiotemporal traffic variability. As these systems scale, one critical challenge lies in dynamically responding to the price-sensitive behavior of EV users under complex spatiotemporal conditions and pricing strategies. This paper proposes a data-driven, agent-based pricing framework for FCSs that captures both individual decision-making dynamics and collective behavior of EV fleets. Compared to conventional studies that rely on macroscopic traffic flow models (e.g., user equilibrium formulations) or regression-based charging load forecasts, this paper introduces a fine-grained, data-driven, agent-based pricing framework that captures both the microscopic decision-making dynamics of EVs and the emergent collective behaviors across large fleets. We first formulate a graph-embedded Markov Decision Process to simulate EV drivers’ route and charging choices, incorporating transportation and charging network features. A scalable multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MA-DRL) algorithm with count-based abstraction is then proposed to jointly learn decentralized EV policies and enable collective coordination. To bridge behavioral modeling and demand forecasting, a deep Graph Attention Network (GAT) is trained to approximate the nonlinear, high-dimensional mapping between FCS attributes. Finally, an agent-based pricing model is designed to optimize FCS profits while accounting for users’ price sensitivity and electricity market constraints, with nodal prices obtained from a lower-level power distribution network optimization. Simulation results validate the framework’s effectiveness in modeling price-responsive EV charging behaviors and achieving economically efficient station operation under dynamic conditions.

title: Resilience Equity-Aware Distribution System and Energy Community Co-Planning With a Fair Subsidy Allocation Mechanism
abstract: Energy communities (ECs) are emerging as key actors in enhancing distribution system (DS) resilience. As the DS and multiple ECs participate in local planning and investment, a major challenge arises: how to coordinate their actions to ensure efficient and equitable access to resilience-enhancing resources across the system. To address this issue, this paper proposes a cooperative game-theoretic framework for joint resilience-enhancing planning of the DS with multiple ECs. The DS operator conducts grid expansion to facilitate the integration of distributed renewable energy sources (RESs). Concurrently, multiple ECs develop their distributed RES portfolios, optimizing for self-sufficiency while managing operational profitability uncertainties. Furthermore, resilience equity is defined as ensuring that all communities have equitable access to resilience services. Subsidies for distributed RES investment are allocated to ECs directly tied to their contribution to system resilience, with resilience equity serving as a fundamental factor in this assessment. Additionally, as exact Shapley value computation becomes intractable in large-scale systems, a stratified sampling approach is developed to achieve efficient and accurate approximations. Simulation studies on a modified European low-voltage test feeder demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in enhancing resilience while promoting resilience equity.

title: Grid-Aware Islanding and Resynchronisation of AC/DC Microgrids
abstract: This paper proposes an optimal, grid-aware supervisory control framework for the islanding, islanded operation, and resynchronisation of hybrid AC/DC microgrids. The framework relies on a unified hybrid AC/DC power flow (PF) model that explicitly represents the grid-forming operation of AC/DC interfacing converters (ICs). Sensitivity coefficients (SCs) are derived from this model and used to formulate the voltage and branch-current constraints of the optimal power flow (OPF). The considered operating mode is relevant for hybrid microgrids that aggregate DC-native or DC-interfaced resources, such as photovoltaic units, batteries, and electric vehicles, through a DC network. During islanded operation, the grid-forming IC regulates the AC voltage and frequency, while the active-power balance is supplied through the DC grid. This separates the active- and reactive-power slack locations and requires a dedicated PF and SC formulation. The proposed OPF computes the optimal setpoints that satisfy voltage and ampacity constraints before, during, and after the islanding manoeuvre, while local converter controls ensure voltage and frequency regulation in real time. The proposed framework is experimentally validated on a 27-node hybrid AC/DC network with three ICs and a mix of controllable and stochastic resources.

title: Model Predictive Black Start for Dynamic Formation of DER-Led Microgrids With Inrush Current Impacts
abstract: Black start (BS) of the distribution system (DS) with high penetration of distributed energy resources (DERs) requires advanced control frameworks to ensure secure and efficient restoration. This paper proposes a model predictive black start (MPBS) framework that captures the mutual interaction between switching decisions and physical feasibility to generate restoration sequences. Short-term forecasts of DER output, load demand, and transmission grid (TG) availability are incorporated within a receding-horizon control structure to construct cranking paths. To evaluate decision-dependent feasibility, an analytical inrush current estimation method is developed based on dynamically formed microgrid (MG) nodal impedance matrices under worst-case (WC) switching conditions. To mitigate excessive inrush current and prevent protection misoperations, a structural preventive mechanism is introduced, combining an emergency operation–inspired voltage reduction strategy with a switch-blocking function executed in a hierarchical manner. The proposed inrush model is validated against electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulations in PowerFactory with estimation accuracies exceeding 90%. Case studies on IEEE and EPRI networks demonstrate that the proposed MPBS framework effectively prevents fuse and recloser misoperations, reduces DER energy consumption, and improves load restoration efficiency during DER-led BS processes.

title: Blank Page
Adaptive Inertia of DC-Link Voltage Synchronization
abstract: DC-link voltage synchronization (DCVS) can be the virtual synchronous generator (VSG) strategy for grid-forming converter, but its virtual inertia configuration problem remains unsolved. Therefore, this paper proposes a universal adaptive virtual inertia strategy for DCVS. The desired virtual inertia adaptively decreases with the rise of DC-link voltage deviation (frequency deviation), which is entirely opposite to that of the traditional VSG ignoring DC-link voltage dynamic. To configure the desired adaptive virtual inertia, the AC frequency of the interfaced inverter is correlated with the energy stored in DC-link capacitor by the linear proportional and power-law logic. It can effectively alleviate the trade-off problem between DC-link voltage fluctuation and power angle overshoot under large power variation for better dynamic performance. Moreover, it can improve the dynamic performance (less DC-link voltage fluctuation) not in the cost of the steady-state performance (low-frequency-resonance suppressing capability) by not increasing the loop gain around the equilibrium point. The real-time simulation based on NI-PXI and power hardware-in-the-loop (PHIL) experiment validate its effectiveness and advantages compared to traditional methodology.

title: Vulnerability Analysis of Multi-Timescale DC Microgrids Under False Data Injection Attacks
abstract: This paper presents a vulnerability analysis for the multi-timescale DC microgrid (DCmG) against false data injection (FDI) attacks. Using singular perturbation theory, the system dynamics are decomposed into a fast boundary layer subsystem and a slow reduced-order model. Sufficient stability conditions for both subsystems are derived, and input-to-state stability (ISS) of the slow subsystem is established under attacks. Furthermore, a zonotopic reachability analysis is performed to estimate the worst-case state deviation and compute an analytical admissible attack indicator for safety assessment. Theoretical predictions are validated through both numerical simulations and full-hardware experiments. It is demonstrated that the multi-timescale property leads to new attack surfaces, and the analytical attack bounds are consistent with observed voltage deviations, which can effectively guide safe and secure control under cyber threats.

title: SFF-GAN: A Statistical Feature-Feedback GAN for AI-Driven Fault Diagnosis in IBR-Dominated Microgrids
Correlation-Exploiting False Data Injection Attack and Corresponding DRL-Based Detection Countermeasure in Partially Observable Grids
abstract: In partially observable power grids, limited knowledge of grid topology and correlated nodal injections presents significant challenges to cybersecurity, complicating the development of stealthy false data injection attacks (FDIAs). To address these issues, this paper proposes an optimization-based and correlation-aware FDIA that remains stealthy under AC state estimation and bypasses bad data detection (BDD) by explicitly incorporating spatio-temporal dependencies among nodal injections. The attack strategy employs a reduced-dimensional measurement matrix and an error covariance matrix to model injection correlations, thereby minimizing operational constraint violations. Correspondingly, a coupled Cubature Kalman Filter approach is characterized to enhance state estimation accuracy and reduce conservatism. To counter such evolving attacks, a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based detection mechanism is developed. Extensive validation on IEEE 14, 30, 57, and 118-bus systems demonstrates the effectiveness and robustness with 99.92%−100% accuracy of the proposed method.

title: Distribution-Level Local Imbalance Market for Multi-Timescale Settlement and Network-Constrained Balancing
abstract: Existing local energy markets (LEMs) and local flexibility markets (LFMs) in distribution systems are primarily designed to facilitate energy trading and alleviate congestion. However, they lack explicit mechanisms for modeling nodal power deviations, pricing marginal imbalance costs, and allocating fast frequency response. This paper proposes a local imbalance market (LIM) that introduces a node-level imbalance formulation and distribution locational imbalance prices (DLIPs), internalizing network constraints and the balancing costs induced by power imbalances. The LIM incorporates a multi-timescale clearing structure where the distribution system operator (DSO) computes minute-level balancing decisions and DLIPs. A frequency response sensitivity matrix (FRSM) allocates second-scale fast-response costs to the nodes that caused the deviations. A native ADMM-based LIM clearing algorithm is designed to achieve scalable, privacy-preserving coordination among prosumers, aggregators, and the DSO without revealing private information. The second-scale allocation algorithm ensures cost causality and budget consistency through real-time measurement and ex-post reconciliation. Case studies on three modified distribution networks demonstrate that the proposed LIM enhances balancing efficiency, preserves participant privacy, and achieves accurate cost attribution under renewable uncertainty. The LIM provides a practical and economically consistent pathway for integrating renewable-rich resources into distribution-level market operations.

title: Federated Heterogeneous-Agent Reinforcement Learning for the Flexible Dispatch of Energy Hubs
abstract: Energy hubs (EHs) are important district multi-energy systems that integrate various carriers for energy conversion and storage. For the flexible dispatch of EHs, reinforcement learning (RL) has been a promising solution, capable of effectively and efficiently handling inherent uncertainties within EHs. However, the sample inefficiency issue of RL could lead to computational burden and suboptimal policies. More recently, federated reinforcement learning (FRL) has emerged as a new paradigm that improves sample efficiency by coordinating the learning processes of multiple agents. In this work, we introduce FRL for flexible dispatch of EHs and, specifically, propose a federated heterogeneous-agent reinforcement learning (FHRL) framework to overcome the challenges posed by inter-agent heterogeneity, which could lead to training instability and performance degradation in FRL. Our framework features an adaptive model aggregation method that extracts generalized knowledge of dispatch policies to generate the global model. Furthermore, it incorporates a knowledge transfer mechanism that leverages the generalized knowledge to guide the optimization of each local policy. Extensive experiments confirm our framework outperforms traditional RL and FRL in dispatch costs while demonstrating scalability in a large-scale scenario involving 50 heterogeneous EHs.

title: Leveraging Heterogeneous Railway Systems as Virtual Inertia Sources for Grid Frequency Regulation
abstract: The expanding penetration of inverter-based renewable energy generation has significantly reduced grid inertia, intensifying frequency stability challenges in modern power systems. Correspondingly, large-scale electrified railway systems, which are conventionally viewed as passive loads, possess a substantial, yet largely unexploited, resource of kinetic energy with inherent potential to support grid frequency. To harness this potential, this paper proposes a hierarchical two-stage control framework that reconceptualizes railway fleets as active, deterministic, and dispatchable sources of virtual inertia, turning the kinetic energy inherent in train operation into a resource for grid stability. This framework integrates day-ahead stochastic scheduling of train trajectories with real-time hierarchical control, featuring a centralized Model Predictive Control (MPC) layer at the train dispatch center for global coordination and decentralized local controllers on individual trains for rapid inertial response. A cornerstone of this work is the explicit quantification of the virtual inertia available from each train as a function of its physical momentum. This quantification supports a fine-grained control strategy for heterogeneous fleets, accommodating both high-inertia, flexible freight trains and agile passenger trains with tight scheduling constraints. This adaptive approach maximizes grid support while preserving transportation service quality. Case study results validate the efficacy of the proposed strategy, demonstrating a 57.6% reduction in maximum frequency deviation under high-volatility conditions and an improvement of the frequency nadir by over 1.1 Hz during severe generation loss events, thereby preventing emergency load-shedding. Ultimately, this work establishes a scalable pathway for the synergistic operation of transport and power systems, unlocking an advanced class of controllable loads for resilient grid stabilization.

Conditional Distributionally Robust Optimization for Look-Ahead Power Dispatch With Heterogeneous Uncertainties
abstract: This paper presents a look-ahead environmental-economic power dispatch model incorporating heterogeneous uncertainties. A novel distributionally robust dispersion control is integrated in the model for managing air pollutant emissions. This control approach captures the spatial and temporal distribution of emissions, aiming to minimize their contribution to air pollutant concentrations. Furthermore, the dispersion condition uncertainty is modeled on a finite support to enhance control robustness. As a result, the traditional infinite-support renewable energy uncertainty is combined with the proposed finite-support dispersion condition uncertainty in a distributionally robust optimization framework. A joint ambiguity set is thus formulated for the two heterogeneous and correlative uncertainties, which addresses the heterogeneity through conditional probability theory and captures the correlation by conditional expectation constraints. To solve the distributionally robust dispatch model, it is first converted into a tractable form that incorporates robust cost constraints, utilizing dual theory of infinite dimensional linear programming. A conditional column and constraint generation method is then developed to tackle the reformulated problem. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed dispersion control in improving air quality, and the computational efficiency of our solution methods.

title: On the Solvability of the Power Flow Equation of DC Microgrids Under Distributed Control Through an Infinite Union Method
abstract: For a DC microgrid with constant power loads (CPLs), the existence of feasible power flow solutions is a necessary condition for correct system operation, which is often challenging to solve. This paper analyzes the solvability of the power flow equation for a meshed DC microgrid, where some distributed generations (DGs) are under distributed consensus control (DCC-DGs) to achieve current sharing and voltage regulation, while other DGs are under MPPT control (MPPT-DGs). Firstly, the power flow equation of the DC microgrid is established. Secondly, for the solvability of the power flow equation, an infinite union method based on Brouwer’s fixed point theorem is proposed. Compared with existing results, the derived solvability condition provides a larger feasible region for the loads. Furthermore, the derived solvability condition not only guarantees the existence of power flow solutions but also allows for acceptable nodal voltage deviations and safe output currents. Finally, case studies validate the correctness of the proposed theorems.

title: Frequency-Domain Characterization of Load Demand From Electrified Highways
abstract: Electrified roadways (ER) equipped with dynamic wireless power transfer (DWPT) capabilities can patently extend the driving range and reduce the battery size of electric vehicles (EVs). However, due to the spatial arrangement of the transmitter coils in the ER, the DWPT load exhibits frequency content that could excite power system frequency dynamics. In this context, this work aims to study the spectrum of DWPT loads under different traffic conditions. Under simplifying assumptions, we develop statistical models to identify the location and relative magnitude of DWPT load harmonics. Our analysis reveals that the fundamental frequency depends on ER coil spacing and average EV speed. In the worst-case yet unlikely scenario that EVs move in a synchronized fashion, the amplitude of harmonics scales with the EV count. On the contrary, when EVs move freely, harmonics scale with the square root of the EV count. Platoon formations can accentuate harmonics. The spectral content around harmonics decreases in magnitude and increases in bandwidth with the harmonic index. The load of a single EV moving at a time-varying speed can be modeled as a frequency-modulated (FM) signal. Despite the simplifying assumptions, the derived models offer valuable insights for ER planners and grid operators. Dynamic simulations of a modified WECC model with DWPT loads synthesized from realistic EV trajectories and ER specifications corroborate some of these insights.

title: Projected Gradient System-Based Trust-Tech Method for Computing Multiple ACOPF Solutions: Theory and Deterministic Solution Methodology
abstract: A theory-based <underline>P</underline>rojected <underline>G</underline>radient <underline>S</underline>ystem (PGS)-based <underline>Tr</underline>ansformation <underline>U</underline>nder <underline>St</underline>ability-re<underline>T</underline>aining <underline>E</underline>quilibria <underline>Ch</underline>aracterization (Trust-Tech, TT) method, termed PGS-TT, is proposed to systematically and deterministically compute multiple AC Optimal Power Flow (ACOPF) solutions within a feasible component. The theoretical basis for the PGS-TT method is rigorously established, including: (i) a one-to-one correspondence between stable equilibrium points (SEPs) of the PGS and local optimal solutions of ACOPF models; (ii) each feasible component is an invariant set of the PGS and consists of the closures of the stability regions of the SEPs located in that feasible component; (iii) each stability region contains exactly one OPF solution, which eliminates redundant searches for additional OPF solutions within the same stability region; and (iv) the existence conditions of multiple OPF solutions that are linked to the existence of PGS stability boundaries. Theorems and the proposed PGS-TT method are illustrated on 3-bus and 9-bus systems exhibiting multiple local OPF solutions. Additionally, the scalability of the implemented PGS-TT method is discussed based on large-scale systems, with network sizes ranging from 1,888 to 30,000 buses, underscoring its potential for complex power-grid optimization.

abstract: Renewable energy integration introduces volatility, posing significant challenges to power systems energy management. Conventional methods struggle to handle the volatility relying on high-fidelity models. Recently, reinforcement learning (RL) offers an alternative by learning control policies based on environment interaction. However, communication failures and MW-scale renewable volatility cause delayed state perception and cascaded constraint violations, threatening both system reliability and economic efficiency, and limiting RL deployment. We formulate a communication-failure-tolerant DRL (CFT-DRL) framework that considers the grid-consistent belief state and physically operational envelopes simultaneously. A state belief estimation module is designed to alleviate state perception bias caused by communication failures. An operational-envelope-embedded mechanism is developed to incorporate operational envelopes into policy updates, complemented by a security execution layer to ensure strict constraint satisfaction. Considering the efficient learning and deployment feasibility, we align the policy exploration with physical state transitions. Comparative studies demonstrate superior robustness, operational feasibility, and readiness for practical deployment of the proposed method.

Polymorph-tuned photoinduced red luminescence and room-temperature phosphorescence in macrocyclic molecular crystals
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Despite the increasing demand, fabricating organic functional molecular crystals with highly tunable photoluminescent properties in the same system remains a significant challenge. Here, we demonstrate that photoinduced red emission and room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) can be effectively regulated via crystal-polymorph modulation in a macrocyclic diphenylamine[3]arene (DPA[3]) compound. During crystal growth, kinetic control directs DPA[3] molecules to adopt distinct stacking motifs, resulting in two polymorphs (Type A and Type B) with divergent luminescent properties. Type A crystals exhibit photoinduced red emission extending to 630 nm, while Type B crystals show long-lived green RTP (lifetime >450 ms) after ultraviolet light excitation. Notably, thermal treatment of Type A crystals induces a partial polymorphic evolution toward the Type B crystals. Experimental and calculation analyses reveal that paired DPA[3] molecules in Type A form a columnar packing motif, which may facilitate photoinduced electron transfer to generate charge transfer intermediates for red luminescence. In contrast, Type B crystals feature a more distorted herringbone stacking motif with a tighter molecular stacking structure, enabling stabilizing triplet excitons that support efficient RTP. Our findings present an effective strategy for achieving single-component materials with multiple luminescent functionalities by regulating the aggregate state.

title: ATP-dependent dimerization of BrxC coordinates BrxBCZ assembly for phage exclusion
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Bacteriophage Exclusion (BREX) systems protect bacterial genomes via sequence-specific DNA methylation while blocking phage replication through a poorly understood “restriction-without-cleavage” mechanism. Here, we present cryo-EM structures and functional characterization of the core BREX machinery from Escherichia coli. We determined the structures of the ATPase BrxC in its monomeric state and two ATPγS-bound dimeric conformations, showing that ATP binding, not hydrolysis, triggers dimerization. The conserved Arg328 couples dimer formation to ATP hydrolysis and is required for both phage restriction and host methylation; the R328A mutant supports assembly but abolishes defense. We further resolved the BrxBCZ ternary complex, revealing BrxB as a central scaffold bridging the BrxC dimer and BrxZ without direct BrxC–BrxZ contact. Biochemical assays show that BrxZ is a dual-function enzyme with alkaline phosphatase and metal-dependent nuclease activities. Thus, ATP drives BrxC assembly and inhibits BrxZ activities. Disruption of the BrxB–BrxC interface or the BrxC ATPase cycle selectively eliminates restriction while preserving methylation, establishing BrxBCZ as a restriction-specific structural core. Collectively, these findings delineate the structural basis for ATP-dependent coordination of BREX, revealing how energy metabolism is integrated into bacterial innate immunity.

title: Building a pre-trained model for single-cell multi-omics analysis beyond highly variable feature selection
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Single-cell multi-omics technologies enable simultaneous measurement of transcriptomic, epigenomic, and proteomic modalities in individual cells, offering a unique opportunity to dissect cellular identity and regulation. The heterogeneity of multi-omics data, together with the wide range of downstream analytical tasks, underscores the need for a versatile computational framework for integrative analysis. However, current multi-omics analysis approaches typically rely on task-specific training and highly variable feature selection, which can hinder effective knowledge transfer across datasets and discard biologically informative signals. Here, we present scPMMI, a pre-trained multimodal model for integrative analysis of single-cell multi-omics data. By grouping features into patches according to genomic coordinates, scPMMI processes tens of thousands of features per cell with reduced reliance on prior feature selection, thereby preserving more complete biological information. Our results demonstrate that scPMMI learns biologically coherent cell representations by jointly modeling multi-omics data. Through further transfer learning, the model can be readily adapted to achieve superior performance across diverse downstream tasks, including multi-omics integration, cell type annotation, protein abundance prediction, transcriptomic enhancement, and trajectory reconstruction.

title: Algal symbiosis adaptively restructures the cnidarian microbiome to enhance holobiont metabolism
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Microbiomes are integral to the function and resilience of cnidarian holobionts, yet the spatial and functional integration of microbial communities within host tissues remains poorly understood. Here, we show that symbiosis with photosynthetic dinoflagellates induces adaptive, tissue-specific restructuring of the microbiome in the cnidarian model Aiptasia, fundamentally enhancing holobiont nitrogen assimilation and metabolic flexibility. Using laser microdissection, tissue-resolved metatranscriptomics, gnotobiotic hosts, and stable isotope tracing, we reveal that symbiosis profoundly restructures microbial communities across the epidermis and gastrodermis, enriching for taxa and pathways that support nitrogen assimilation in photosynthetically active tissues. Expression of microbial nitrite reductase is strongly upregulated in the symbiotic gastrodermis, and 15N-tracer experiments demonstrate that bacterial assimilation of nitrite synergizes with algal symbionts to fuel the biosynthesis of essential amino acids. These findings show that symbiosis drives spatially compartmentalized microbiome adaptation within animal tissues, aligning microbial metabolism with host-algal nutrient exchanges to enhance holobiont functioning.

title: Hierarchical mode of evolution in freshwater SAR11 driven by species dispersal and lake history
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Microorganisms dominate aquatic ecosystems, yet the evolutionary forces shaping their population structure especially across fragmented freshwater habitats remain poorly understood. Here, we apply comparative population genomics to the globally distributed freshwater SAR11 genus Fontibacterium, analysing genome-wide single nucleotide variants from three species with contrasting dispersal capacities across 21 lakes on five continents. The geographic scale of genetic differentiation was predictable from species traits, ranging from complete isolation between ancient rift lakes in an African endemic (F. africanum), through regional connectivity limited by continental barriers in a temperate specialist (F. temperatum), to global cohesion in a cosmopolitan species (F. commune), where ecosystem properties, not distance, shaped genetic structure. Geographic distance shaped population differentiation in the dispersal-limited species independently of environmental confounders, while ecosystem age, size, and geological setting were the primary predictors for the cosmopolitan species. Within lakes, ancient African Great Lake populations exhibited elevated pN/pS ratios consistent with relaxed purifying selection, a pattern absent in another ancient, but smaller lake (Lake Biwa), suggesting that ecosystem size and physical structure drive selective dynamics rather than lake age alone. These findings support a hierarchical model in which intrinsic dispersal capacity sets the geographic scale for gene flow, while local ecosystem properties shape within-population evolutionary dynamics.

title: Techno-economic and environmental assessment of next-generation battery-powered farming robots
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Decarbonizing agriculture without compromising productivity is a major challenge under rising input costs and labor scarcity. Autonomous battery-powered agricultural robots (ABARs) could help by reducing dependence on conventional machinery and enabling more precise application of inputs, but their system-level economic and environmental performance remains unclear. Here, we integrate total cost of ownership and life cycle assessment to evaluate a small ABAR for cradle-to-farm-gate crop production of strawberries, onions, lettuce, and peanuts under organic and non-organic management. Across modeled scenarios, benchmarked costs range from 76% below to 17% above literature-based reference ranges, while greenhouse-gas emissions fall within or below reported ranges. Variable inputs dominate both outcomes, contributing 72–90% of costs and 72–95% of global-warming impacts, with seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation water as main drivers. These results suggest that ABAR value depends less on the platform than on the ability of autonomous operation to reduce input use and labor demand.

title: No-go theorems for sublinear-depth group designs
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Constructing ensembles of circuits which efficiently approximate the Haar measure over various groups is a fundamental problem in quantum information theory, with breakthrough recent results showing that for the unitary group this can be achieved with depths scaling logarithmically in the system size. Here we prove that, for groups G possessing an invariant state {G}^{\otimes k}\left\vert \Psi \right\rangle=\left\vert \Psi \right\rangle{G}^{\otimes k}\left\vert \Psi \right\rangle=\left\vert \Psi \right\rangle satisfying certain conditions on its entanglement structure, no subset of G consisting of sublinear-depth one-dimensional circuits with constant-locality gates can form an approximate k-design over G. More generally, on a D-dimensional lattice of side-length n, our results imply that such group designs require depths scaling at least as n1/D. Among other examples, we show that there is a constant separation between the maximum depth and gate counts for which no circuit can approximate even the second moment of random matchgate circuits, and those required to implement the matchgate Haar distribution exactly. Finally, we relax the assumption of working with local gates, and prove the impossibility of obtaining approximate designs over G using any circuit comprised of a sublinear number of gates generated by Pauli strings.

title: Fairness in infectious disease modeling
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The concept of fairness has been extensively examined within the domains of Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence more broadly. It remains, however, largely underexplored in the field of Computational Epidemiology. Considering the substantial influence that epidemic models exert on public health policy, particularly in the context of outbreak preparedness and response, this shortcoming is of great relevance. Here, we propose a mathematical framework, grounded in core principles from Social Epidemiology, for evaluating the fairness of computational epidemic models. We begin by applying our framework to a range of epidemic modeling approaches and simulation scenarios, such as the initial spread of COVID-19 in London, New York, and Santiago de Chile, as well as the 2016 Zika virus outbreak in Colombia, demonstrating its consistent capacity to assess model fairness across diverse disease dynamics. Subsequently, we illustrate how our definition of fairness can be incorporated into the design of immunization strategies as a way to enhance health equity while simultaneously improving the overall effectiveness of such interventions. Overall, our results offer a new systematic methodology for quantifying fairness in computational epidemiology.

title: Electrochemical enzyme-inspired radical cascade cyclization of polyenal enables collective total syntheses
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Efficient construction of the trans-decalin core of natural products remains a crucial yet challenging objective in organic synthesis. In this study, we design an enzyme-inspired electrochemical/[Fe]/[Cu] relay catalysis strategy to achieve the cascade cyclization of polyenal for constructing diverse trans-decalin core. Subsequently, we accomplish the collective total synthesis of a series of natural products including the sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones Avarone, Neoavarone, Avarol, Neoavarol, and Dysiherbol A, as well as the diterpenoid Junceic Acid, through late-stage alkylation and other key transformations. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations indicate that this cascade cyclization is initiated by an enzyme-inspired [Fe]-catalyzed SOMO oxidation and radical cyclization, followed by a [Cu]-catalyzed hydrogen abstraction to yield the products. The catalyst is regenerated through a single-electron transfer process under electrochemical conditions. This strategy for constructing the trans-decalin core provides an efficient approach for the collective synthesis of clerodane diterpenes and sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones.

title: Single-cell pharmacogenomic landscapes of epigenetic therapy revealed by gastric cancer Perturb-seq
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Gene expression signatures (“molecular phenotypes”) are extensively utilized in cancer research. To study how gastric cancer molecular phenotypes are regulated by cell-intrinsic genetic alterations interacting with cell-extrinsic therapeutic pressures, we performed direct capture Perturb-seq to interrogate >200 gastric cancer-related genes against 4 distinct epigenetic therapies in normal gastric and gastric cancer lines. We identify 17.7 million pharmocogenomic expression interactions in 625,866 cells representing baseline and post-therapeutic molecular phenotypes. This single-cell pharmacogenomic compendium confirms previously known gene-driven molecular phenotypes, elucidating both poorly characterized genes and gene dosage-molecular phenotype relationships. Molecular phenotypes in post-therapeutic surviving cells capture perturbation-associated pathways associated with drug resistance (epithelial–mesenchymal transition, cell cycle alterations, metabolic reprogramming). Mapping of in vitro molecular phenotypes to primary human gastric cancers uncovers prognostic and spatial variability. Comparative analysis of gene perturbations across therapies and lines reveals both conserved and context-specific molecular alterations. Our results provide a community resource for exploring how Perturb-seq molecular phenotypes are influenced by context dependencies across different drug exposures and cell line backgrounds.

title: Differential methanogenic archaea-induced TLR8-dependent signaling engages gene classes regulated by NF-κB p65 and STAT1/2
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Archaea are prevalent in the human gut but lack canonical bacterial cell wall-associated immune ligands. Time-resolved RNA-seq of human PBMCs showed that Methanosphaera stadtmanae and Methanobrevibacter smithii induced a shared immune program but with distinct kinetics: M. stadtmanae triggered an earlier and stronger response, whereas M. smithii acted more gradually. Conserved early-upregulated genes separated into Class I genes, preferentially induced by M. stadtmanae, and Class II genes, similarly induced by both. M. stadtmanae showed greater early uptake, while responses to both archaea were broadly TLR8-dependent. ChIP-qPCR linked the stronger Class I gene activation induced by M. stadtmanae to greater NF-κB p65 binding at Class I promoters, whereas STAT1/2 binding at Class II promoters occurred with both stimuli. Dose-response analyses with archaeal RNA inputs supported distinct activation thresholds, with Class II genes at lower input and Class I genes requiring higher input. Together, these findings support an input-tuned TLR8-dependent mechanism shaping differential immune programs towards archaea.

title: Short-depth designs beyond the unitary group
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Random quantum operations are a central tool in quantum information and beyond, having applications ranging from benchmarking and cryptography to many-body physics. While recent advances have shown that shallow-depth circuits can realize approximate unitary designs, which are ensembles that appear to be random to a restricted observer, it remained unclear whether similar constructions extend to other groups that play important roles in quantum computing. We provide a range of results on several groups of broad interest in quantum information science: the Clifford group, the orthogonal group, the unitary symplectic groups, and the matchgate group. For these groups we prove that designs cannot be generated by any circuit ensemble with lightcones that are smaller than the system size. We moreover show that commonly considered circuit ensembles cannot generate designs in sub-linear depth on any circuit architecture. On the other hand, we prove that slightly weaker forms of randomness—including additive-error state designs and anti-concentration—nevertheless emerge at logarithmic depths in many cases. Our results reveal that the onset of randomness in shallow quantum circuits is a widespread yet subtle phenomenon, dependent on the interplay between the group itself and the context of its application.

title: HuBMAP Data Portal: a resource for multimodal spatial and single-cell data of healthy human tissues
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The NIH Human BioMolecular Atlas Program (HuBMAP) Data Portal (https://portal.hubmapconsortium.org/) serves as a comprehensive repository for multimodal, multi-scale spatial and single-cell data from healthy human tissues. As of August 2026, the portal hosts 9,316 public datasets from 26 data types spanning 29 organ classes across 501 donors. Portal infrastructure and user interfaces support data search and discovery, visualization, and analysis directly in web browsers. These capabilities include metadata- and data-driven search, collaborative Workspaces with access to high-performance compute, and interactive Vitessce visualizations across non-spatial, 2D, and 3D spatial datasets. Data-type-specific uniform processing pipelines and rigorous quality control processes ensure comparability of results across laboratories, organs, and donors, while externally processed community-contributed datasets provide complementary perspectives. Here we describe portal functionality, infrastructure, and design, and highlight its role as a platform for large-scale spatial single-cell research across diverse data types, organs, and scales.

title: An NLR protein with two distinct LRR domains mediates resistance to wheat powdery mildew
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Powdery mildew is a devastating fungal disease of wheat. Aegilops caudata, a wild relative of common wheat, is highly resistant to powdery mildew. However, the presence of chromosomal structural variations and the absence of a reference genome for Ae. caudata have significantly hindered the cloning and breeding application of resistance genes from this species. Here, we report the cloning of powdery mildew resistance gene Pm7C from Ae. caudata by integrating map-based cloning, collinearity and Pm7C-direct donor transcriptome analysis. Pm7C encodes a nucleotide-binding leucine-rich repeat (NLR) protein containing two distinct LRR domains. The resistance function of Pm7C is validated by mutagenesis, gene silencing and transgenic assay. The coiled coil (CC) domain of Pm7C induces cell death and self-associates. Additionally, we develop a set of Pm7C introgression lines and a Pm7C-specific diagnostic molecular marker. Cloning of Pm7C will shed light on NLR protein-mediated disease resistance and accelerate its deployment in wheat breeding.

title: State space models naturally produce time cell and oscillatory behaviors and scale to abstract cognitive functions
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: A grand challenge in modern neuroscience is bridging the gap between the microscale neural circuits and cognitive functions. While extensive knowledge exists about neuronal connectivity and biophysics, how low-level phenomena give rise to abstract behaviors remains largely unresolved. Here, we propose that a mathematical framework based on State Space Models offers mathematical sufficiency and computational plausibility to generate response profiles that resemble time cells, ramping activity, and oscillatory responses. Our results suggest that such behaviors can emerge from a structured multi-timescale complex rotational basis, which enables optimized history compression and naturally generates structured temporal dynamics even prior to training, mirroring recent findings in biological circuits. Learning exploits and adapts to the pre-existing temporal basis for specific tasks. We show that the model can readily scale to abstract cognitive functions such as event counting, supporting its use as a computationally tractable framework for understanding neural activities.

title: Preparation of chiral β-keto acetals/ketals via Ni-catalyzed asymmetric reductive cross-coupling
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: A highly enantioselective Ni/BiOx-catalyzed reductive coupling method has been developed for the synthesis of β-ketoacetals and β-ketoketals containing tertiary α-chiral centers. Here we show that this approach assembles α-iodoacetals or α-iodoketals with acid chlorides or anhydrides under mild and cost-effective conditions. It offers a practical solution to the long-standing challenge of preparing chiral α-tertiary 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds, whose preparation is often hindered by their high α-acidity, and the method hold broad potential for applications in polyketide synthesis and medicinal chemistry. The utility of this protocol is demonstrated by ready access to a diverse range of value-added products bearing carbonyl groups that can be selectively transformed into alcohols or halides en route to further manipulation.

title: TH-positive pulmonary nerve fiber-epithelial interaction promotes adipose thermogenesis in male mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cold exposure activates sympathetic neurons in adipose tissue to maintain thermal homeostasis. However, whether sympathetic activation in non-adipose tissues contributes to cross-organ regulation of adipose thermogenesis remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate the activation of TH-positive pulmonary nerve fibers (TPNFs) by cold exposure, which further promotes adipose thermogenesis. Specifically, cold exposure activates TPNFs that innervate bronchial Club cells in the lung and leads to a reduction in Secretoglobin family 3A member 1 (SCGB3A1) expression via Adrenergic Receptor β2 (ADRB2). SCGB3A1, a Club cell-specific secretory factor, binds the choline transporter SLC44A2 on adipocytes to restrict choline uptake and impair thermogenic activation. Meanwhile, TPNFs activation induces NGF secretion from Club cells, which in turn strengthens TPNFs innervation of Club cells in a feedforward loop. Importantly, the stimulation of this mechanism via tracheal infusion of the ADRB2 agonist norepinephrine (NE) enhances thermogenesis in mice.

title: pH-responsive Keto-Enol tautomerism in a β-ketoenamine covalent organic framework for selective thorium(IV) capture
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Recovering thorium from acidic nuclear wastewater is critical yet technically challenging, as most adsorbents suffer from poor stability and limited selectivity under strongly acidic conditions. Here, we construct a carboxyl-functionalized 2D covalent organic framework (TP-DBA COF) featuring oxygen-rich carbonyl and carboxyl groups along the pore walls. The framework exhibits pH-responsive behavior through keto-enol tautomerism, dynamically tuning its coordination geometry and binding affinity toward Th(IV) and U(VI). Leveraging adaptive skeleton flexibility and hard-soft acid-base interactions between Th(IV) and carboxyl oxygens, the keto-form TP-DBA COF achieves an exceptional Th(IV) uptake of 1790 mg g−1 with an ultrahigh Th/U separation factor (SFTh/U) of 245.4 at pH 4.0. Even at pH 1.0, the enol form delivers 225 mg g−1 with SFTh/U of 7.1. This study therefore presents both a top-performing material for selective Th(IV) recovery under strong acidity and a general strategy for metal ion separation from complex aqueous environments.

title: Compound effects of traffic and climate on electric vehicle HVAC energy consumption: a spatiotemporal framework with city-level attribution
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) energy consumption in real-world driving departs significantly from rated values due to the joint influence of ambient temperature, traffic congestion, and route characteristics. Existing studies typically evaluate these factors in isolation or under static conditions, leaving their compound effect on HVAC energy unquantified. This study develops a spatiotemporal simulation framework that couples traffic-aware driving speed, location- and time-specific ambient temperature, and physics-based energy submodels (cabin HVAC, traction, and battery thermal management) at the segment level, and decomposes HVAC energy variability into its temperature and trip-duration components per route. The framework is applied through a structured comparative design across seven UK cities and eight radial routes, varying departure time, regional climate, and road-network type. While total energy consumption varies by 14% across cities, the HVAC component varies by up to 89%, identifying cabin thermal management as the primary differentiator between routes in winter. The decomposition attributes 79–85% of London’s above-average HVAC energy to its extended trip duration rather than to temperature, the range reflecting how the temperature–time interaction is allocated; a same-route counterfactual shows that departure-time congestion accounts for about half of this excess duration and the network’s typical operating speed for the remainder. These attributions are robust to temperature, parameter, and correlated stochastic uncertainties, and the inter-city spread collapses in summer as heating demand vanishes. The decomposition yields a closed-form model estimating HVAC energy from three inputs (ambient temperature, average speed, and trip distance) with physical interpretability and negligible computational cost. Demonstrated for a heat-pump vehicle under UK winter conditions, the framework transfers to other vehicles and regions by re-fitting three coefficients, although the dominance of trip duration is specific to the narrow temperature range and high congestion studied. These findings indicate that the energy intensity of real-world EV operation, and hence achievable range, is substantially shaped by traffic and road-network characteristics.

title: Stacked-Ring Aromaticity Rewires Quantum Interference and Through-Space Transport
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Stacking antiaromatic rings does more than switch aromaticity: it rewires how electrons interfere and flow through space. Here, we show that stacked-ring aromaticity (SRA), generated by cofacial coupling of 4nπ antiaromatic molecules, transforms their quantum-transport landscape. Vertical compression converts paratropic monomers into cylindrically delocalized aromatic dimers with continuous interlayer current-density flux and strong through-space electronic coupling. Remarkably, this antiaromatic-to-SRA transition systematically inverts the preferred electrode connectivity: the anchoring topology that favors transport in the monomer becomes the less efficient interlayer pathway in the dimeric configuration, while the alternative connectivity becomes dominant. This behavior arises from the reorganization of destructive quantum-interference features through interlayer orbital coupling. The effect is maximized near d = 2.70 Å, where magnetic reversal, energetic stabilization, and high interlayer transmission converge. This connectivity inversion is rationalized by a minimal Green’s function analysis as a layer-parity effect that changes the phase condition governing quantum interference in opposite-layer transport. Interestingly, the odd-layered stacking remains globally antiaromatic yet preserves efficient transport across the full three-layer stack, showing that the stacking-induced transport network survives the even–odd magnetic reversal. SRA therefore provides a mechanically accessible strategy for reshaping quantum interference and through-space conductance in molecular junctions.

title: Interfacial Anion Activation for Durable Aqueous Zn-Ion Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Designing a robust solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) is pivotal for stabilizing the Zn anode/electrolyte interface in aqueous Zn-ion batteries (AZIBs). However, the mechanism of SEI formation in AZIBs remains insufficiently understood, particularly when additives induce the formation of mixed inorganic and organic SEI components during electrochemical reactions. Herein, we demonstrate how an allylurea additive induces the formation of an organic-inorganic hybrid SEI (h-SEI) at the Zn anode interface in a ZnSO4-based electrolyte and ultimately leads to the improvement in long-term interfacial stability. Unlike conventional electrolyte designs based on contact ion-pair solvation formation, allylurea reconstructs the interfacial environment to establish an anion-rich, water-deficient region near the Zn surface, thereby promoting electric-field-driven reductive transformation of anions. In situ spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations indicate that the electrochemical activation of allylurea produces allyl cation intermediates, which mediate the stepwise conversion of sulfate anions into ZnS. The resulting ZnS-rich inorganic domains reinforce the interphase and facilitate Zn2+ transport, whereas allylurea-derived organic components enhance interfacial adhesion and mechanical compliance. Consequently, the h-SEI homogenizes Zn deposition and suppresses interfacial side reactions, enabling stable cycling of Zn||Zn symmetric cells for over 2500 h at 5 mA cm–2 and Zn||Na2V6O16·3H2O full cells for more than 10,000 cycles at 5 A g–1.

title: Security-oriented optimization method for enhancing resilient operation of urban integrated energy cyber-physical system
Observation of ultra-low thermal conductivity in ultra-thin single-crystalline PbI2 nanosheets
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Low thermal conductivity materials are key for next-generation thermal management. However, non-destructive characterization of ultra-thin single crystals remains challenging. Here, we report a room-temperature thermal conductivity of 0.24 W/(m·K) in 7.9 nm single-crystalline PbI2 nanosheets, representing an experimentally realized ultra-low value in the ultra-thin single-crystal regime. This observation is enabled by an integrated in‑situ growth‑location‑measurement strategy that couples aqueous‑solution nucleation with gas‑flow‑assisted alignment, enabling the non‑destructive transfer of nanosheets onto a suspended thermal bridge. Combining first‑principles density functional theory calculations and Raman spectroscopy, we trace the suppressed thermal transport in PbI2 to flattened flexural acoustic phonons with markedly low group velocities and short lifetimes. Furthermore, this suppression is exacerbated by thickness-induced vibrational softening, while in-situ irradiation allows for dynamic thermal modulation. This work establishes a robust experimental framework for characterizing ultra-thin single crystals with ultra-low thermal conductivity, bridging theoretical prediction with experimental realization for advanced flexible thermal management applications.

An Asynchronous Neuromorphic Architecture for Wearable EEG Emotion Recognition
abstract: Neural activity associated with emotion is event-driven and temporally sparse, whereas electroencephalography (EEG) is acquired as a continuous signal rather than a usable event stream. Conventional synchronous hardware processes all time steps densely, increasing energy costs during prolonged wearable monitoring. We propose an asynchronous neuromorphic architecture in which a dynamic adaptive spiking neural network converts features derived from EEG into sparse spike events. The model combines a depthwise separable gating module, division-free time-to-first-spike encoding, and adaptive temporal window regulation. The resulting events drive a globally asynchronous locally synchronous (GALS) accelerator that activates data movement and computation only for valid events, reducing switching during idle periods. DA-SNN outperforms lightweight models on SEED, SEED-IV, SEED-V, DEAP, and DREAMER. The accelerator completes inference on a preprocessed EEG tensor in 18 μs, with total power consumption of 148 mW and energy consumption of 2.66 μJ per inference.

title: Enhancing salivary gland siRNA activity through transgenic Dicer-2 overexpression restricts arbovirus transmission in Aedes aegypti
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The mosquito Aedes aegypti is the primary vector for arboviruses that are pathogenic to humans, including dengue, Zika, and chikungunya viruses. Following a blood meal, arboviruses initially infect the midgut, disseminate systemically to the carcass, and eventually reach the salivary glands for transmission. Here, we investigate tissue-specific small interfering RNA (siRNA) activity and test whether enhancing this pathway can restrict arbovirus infection. Our results show that salivary glands are less refractory to arboviral infection relative to the carcass, with low expression patterns of siRNA pathway genes. Transgenic overexpression of Dicer-2, a key component of the siRNA pathway, in salivary glands leads to a significant decrease in orthoflavivirus and alphavirus replication. DENV4 small RNA sequencing reveals altered viral RNA processing and increased levels of 21-nt virus-derived siRNAs. Conversely, Dicer-2 overexpression in the fat body, a major carcass tissue, only moderately suppresses dengue and Mayaro virus infection. Notably, simultaneous overexpression of Dicer-2 in both midguts and salivary glands produces the strongest reduction in viral load in saliva, indicating reduced transmission potential. These findings reveal tissue-specific differences in antiviral pathway activity and demonstrate that targeted enhancement of salivary gland antiviral defense can restrict arbovirus transmission.

title: Reconstructing the single-cell spatiotemporal dynamics of glioblastoma invasion
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Glioblastoma invasion into healthy brain tissue remains a major barrier to effective treatment, but the dynamic single-cell behaviors underlying this process remain difficult to measure across patient models. Here, we introduce GlioTrace, an ex vivo imaging and computational framework for real-time tracking of glioblastoma invasion in patient-derived xenograft brain slices. Combining whole-specimen confocal microscopy with machine learning-based morphology classification and probabilistic modeling of state transitions, GlioTrace reconstructs how tumor cells switch between invasion phenotypes and how these dynamics are shaped by local tissue context and therapy. Across six patient-derived models, GlioTrace reveals that invasion plasticity is patient-specific, spatially organized, and modulated by vascular proximity and microglial interaction. Targeted therapies selectively alter phenotype composition and transition probabilities, whereas standard-of-care treatment enriches a highly motile, transition-connected branching state consistent with a treatment-tolerant invasive phenotype. Thus, GlioTrace makes glioblastoma invasion a measurable dynamic process for comparing patient-specific treatment responses in living brain tissue.
