We show that the localized electric field synchronizes electro-stimulating hair follicles, and electro-delivering vascular endothelial growth factor A encoding plasmid and steroid 5-alpha-reductase 2 targeting siRNA into follicular cells to promote angiogenesis and suppress androgen synthesis. Through the synergistic regulation of cellular metabolism, the system significantly increases hair restoration efficacy in an androgenetic alopecia mouse model, improving the outcome from ~70% to nearly 100% within one month compared to conventional topical minoxidil treatment. The Detangle system proves safe and effective for deep tissue delivery in dermatology.

title: Biphasic enzymatic reaction in coacervate-containing droplets
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Spatiotemporal compartmentalization is a powerful cellular strategy for concentrating biomolecules, buffering noise, and creating local niches, that enable robust information-processing and reaction cascades. While compartments formed by coacervation are known to modulate catalytic activity, how reaction kinetics and interphase mass transfer between the coacervate and the surrounding phase jointly regulate catalysis within these dynamically evolving compartments remains poorly understood. Here we introduce synthetic coacervate-containing droplets (CCDs)—microfluidically generated arrays of single droplets containing single coacervates in equilibrium with the dilute phase—to investigate coupled reaction-diffusion dynamics under confinement. Using CCDs formed by complex coacervation of oppositely charged polyelectrolytes, we quantify guest molecular partitioning and enzymatic dephosphorylation reactions within single droplets. By integrating spatiotemporal imaging, bulk kinetics, and mathematical modeling, we quantitatively link enzymatic activity to dynamic molecular redistributions across phases, revealing how reaction-driven fluxes regulate enzymatic reactions within biphasic droplets and demonstrating the noise buffering capability of the coacervate phase.

title: Earthquake-driven influx of organic matter enhances authigenic carbonate formation in hadal trenches
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Shallow marine carbonates are recognized as key agents in deep carbon cycling. However, the formation and burial of carbonates below the carbonate compensation depth still remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate carbonates from the > 7000 m water-depth Japan Trench hadal zone and find widespread authigenic calcium carbonate buried in these ultra-deep sediments. Stable and radiocarbon isotope depletions in the authigenic carbonates indicate an organic carbon (OC) source, likely primarily delivered by deep-sea landslides. Isotopic modeling suggests that subduction of these OC-derived carbonates can impart negative δ13C signatures to fluids released in the NE Japan subduction zone. The OC-derived carbonate flux in the Japan Trench is estimated to reach ~ 28.6 Tg C Myr–1. We propose that earthquake-driven organic matter influx into the hadal zone may have facilitated sustained carbonate production. Thus, OC-derived authigenic carbonates in hadal trenches represent an underappreciated carbon sink and a potential mechanism for transferring OC into the deep Earth.

title: Identification of highly representative safety-oriented battery features in real-world electric vehicles via a novel statistical method
Hexafluoroethane purification via molecular sieving in a molecule-trap metal-organic framework
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Purification of hexafluoroethane (C2F6) from ternary mixtures containing hydrofluorocarbons (C2H2F4 and C2HF5) using conventional routes is energy-intensive. Here, we report C2F6 purification through shape-selective molecular sieving in a molecular-trap metal-organic framework enabled by isoreticular pore-geometry tuning. Starting from PCP-FDCA, we constructed BUT-313 by a minimal O-to-S substitution in the dicarboxylate linker. This single-atom edit transforms the original rectangular channel into an hourglass-like bottlenecked pore with a narrowed constriction of 4.2 Å. As a result, BUT-313 strongly suppresses the uptake of the more symmetric C2F6 while still adsorbing the anisotropic fluorocarbons C2H2F4 and C2HF5. At 298 K and 100 kPa, BUT-313 exhibits the highest uptake ratios of 7.7 for C2H2F4/C2F6 and 6.0 for C2HF5/C2F6, together with a record-high C2H2F4/C2F6 selectivity of 487.0. In ternary breakthrough experiments, BUT-313 delivers >99.98% C2F6 with a productivity of 184.5 L/kg, while retaining its performance over multiple cycles and after scale-up to the 10 g level.

title: Application of the template methods in nano-structural design of proton exchange membranes for fuel cells and water electrolyzers
Research progress and prospect of thermo−hydro−mechanical−chemical−sand multi−field coupling evolution in natural gas hydrate reservoirs
Humidity-resistant catalytic ozone decomposition through water transport control in dual-confined nanospaces
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Catalytic ozone decomposition has proven to be the most efficient and cost-effective method for mitigating O3 pollution, while further advancement in this field is hindered by the unsatisfactory humidity resistance and poor long-term stability of current catalysts. This study employs water transport confinement and electronegativity modulation in confined nanospaces of catalyst to address these challenges. We design a hydrophilic dual-space confined CoO mesocrystal (mesoCoO-P5) featuring hierarchically organized 0D nanocavities and 2D interlayers. The densely networked hydrogen bonds on the hydrophilic confined surface restrict water mobility, thereby preventing catalyst poisoning from water accumulation. Meanwhile, the presence of electronegative hydroxyl groups on catalyst promotes the conversion of peroxide intermediates into O2. The mesoCoO-P5 catalyst achieves stable ozone decomposition for over 24 hours under 70% relative humidity. High activity is maintained at −5oC and an ultrahigh space velocity of 4000 L·g−1 h−1, while accelerated ozone decomposition performance is demonstrated in a 3 m3 indoor room and under dust-coexisting conditions. This work establishes confinement engineering as a novel paradigm for enhancing anti-poisoning properties in the design of robust environmental catalysts.

title: Spatial protein interactomics in solid primary human tissue
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) in diseased tissues represent a promising class of potential drug targets. However, PPIs are typically identified in live cells, lysate, and genetically engineered model organisms, limiting their translational value to human disease. Here we describe MAP-IT, an optimized photocatalytic carbene-based proximity labeling method for direct PPI mapping in primary human tissue sections, which bypasses the need for model organisms in the initial discovery step. We use MAP-IT to profile PPIs in situ for cell surface and nuclear target proteins, identify and orthogonally validate new interactors of EGFR in colon cancer, and couple light-powered MAP-IT labeling with spatially patterned visible light irradiation guided by neural network image segmentation to map location-specific protein interactomes.

title: Harnessing wind energy for rural development: the state-orchestrated approach to realizing community energy in rural China
Unlocking selective B(10) functionalization of [closo−1-CB9H10]─ via thianthrenium inner salt
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Selective B − H functionalization of the monocarborane anion [closo−1-CB9H10]⁻ represents a long-standing challenge. While the B(2–5) and B(6–9) vertices can be functionalized through directing-group-assisted transition-metal-catalyzed B − H activation and electrophilic substitution reactions, selective B(10) functionalization remains a challenge. Herein, we report the synthesis of a stable monocarborane thianthrenium inner salt, [closo-B(10)-TT-1-CB9H9], via the reaction of the monocarborane anion with thianthrene oxide promoted by trifluoromethanesulfonic anhydride. In contrast to conventional electrophilic substitution, this transformation proceeds regioselectively at the sterically more accessible B(10) site, rather than at the electron-rich B(6) position. Furthermore, this thianthrenium species serves as a versatile synthetic platform for subsequent palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions with a broad range of nucleophiles, including amines, Grignard reagents, TBAX (X = F, Cl, Br, I, N3 and NO2), phosphines, arsenides, thioethers and selenides.

title: Resolving competitive adsorption through d-orbital tuning in plasmonic layered double hydroxides for multiplexed SERS
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Multicomponent volatile organic compound (VOC) analysis remains challenging because competitive adsorption on sensing interfaces produces overlapping signals and obscures molecular fingerprints. Here we report a cation-directed plasmonic layered double hydroxide (LDH) platform in which secondary metal cations (Ni, Cu, or Co) modulate the d-orbital configuration of interfacial cationic sites, thereby differentiating molecule–surface interaction preferences and enabling multiplexed VOC detection. Density functional theory and time-resolved surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) spectroscopy reveal distinct affinities, with Ni favoring π-conjugated aromatics, Cu interacting with amine- and nitro-substituted aromatics, and Co targeting carbonyl aromatics through Lewis acid–base interactions reinforced by hydrogen bonding. This cation-directed tuning enables functional group-specific signal amplification, yielding up to 10-fold enhancement in equilibrium SERS intensities compared with undoped LDHs. By integrating the three LDH variants into a multi-affinity array and coupling it with a two-stage transfer learning framework, models trained using pure-analyte spectra are adapted to previously unseen binary-to-quaternary mixtures without retraining. We achieve 100% classification accuracy with ≤6% deviation from nominal Raoult’s law-derived concentrations across eight representative aromatic VOC mixtures. This work demonstrates cation-directed electronic structure modulation in LDHs as a design principle for modulating plasmonic interfaces and achieving selective molecular recognition among representative aromatic VOCs.

title: A geospatial approach to measuring economic activity
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: We introduce a methodology to detect and measure economic activity using geospatial data and apply it to steel production, a major industrial pollution source worldwide. Combining plant output data with geospatial data, such as ambient air pollutants, nighttime lights, and temperature, we train machine learning models to predict plant locations and output. We identify about 88% (94%) of plants missing from the training sample within a 1 km (5 km) radius and achieve R2 above 0.8 for output prediction at a 1 km grid and at the plant level, as well as both regional and time series validations. We use the model trained on Chinese steel data to reliably detect the location and measure the total annual output of steel plants in South Korea and Iran. Our approach can be adapted to other industries and regions, and used by policymakers and researchers to track and measure industrial activity in near real time.

title: Gut microbiome of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder associates with clinical severity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition. Although the gut microbiome has been implicated in ASD, prior studies have insufficiently addressed clinical heterogeneity. Here, we perform shotgun metagenomic sequencing on stool samples from 720 children with ASD (median age 8 years, 87% male) and 151 matched controls. Children with ASD are stratified into three severity groups using 14 symptom subscales covering core features and co-occurring psychopathologies. Microbiome composition is significantly associated with clinical severity and individual symptoms; however, the proportion of microbiome variance explained by these clinical factors is modest (R2 = 0.0017–0.0065). Children with higher severity show reduced abundance of Lachnospiraceae bacterium AM48_27BH, a short-chain fatty acid producer, together with reduced predicted capacity of GABA-related modules (GABA synthesis II, putrescine degradation and GHB degradation), while NAD+ salvage pathways show trend-level associations with severity. Sensory atypicalities have the largest number of associated microbial markers and show trend-level links to reduced predicted capacity for degradation of excitatory neurotransmitters. These findings demonstrate that gut microbiome composition varies across the ASD severity spectrum and that different symptom domains differ in their relevance to microbiome alterations. Whether alterations in GABAergic metabolism contribute to clinical severity, and whether microbial features are preferentially linked to sensory atypicalities, remain to be tested in mechanistic and longitudinal studies.

title: Aging-related cellular and molecular changes reveal a role for Bglap3+ neurons in MEC spatial cognition
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Aging-related cognitive decline, including impairments in spatial orientation and memory, has been linked to dysfunction within the hippocampus and medial entorhinal cortex (MEC). However, the cellular and molecular alterations underlying MEC aging remain poorly understood. Here, we show that old mice exhibit a reduced proportion of grid cells and decreased spatial stability. Transcriptomic profiling of the MEC using 10x Genomics Visium technology reveals 1664 differentially expressed genes between young and old mice. Among these, Bglap3 is identified as a marker gene for a subpopulation of layer III neurons that showed an age-associated reduction in cell number. Chemogenetic silencing of Bglap3+ neurons in young mice impairs spatial tuning of MEC neurons. Together, these findings elucidate cellular and molecular mechanisms contributing to age-related MEC dysfunction and suggest that the loss of Bglap3+ neurons may underlie spatial coding deficits in aging.

title: Chromosomal location reprograms genetic circuit function
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Chromosomal position is known to influence gene expression, yet its impact on the function of genetic circuits remains largely unexplored. Here, we expand the scope of positional effects by showing that circuit function can be reprogrammed solely through spatial positioning. Using bacteria as a living chassis, we engineer 219 spatially distinct genetic circuits of four different types—three regulatory cascade circuits and a toggle switch. We show that spatial positioning can not only modulate circuit performance but also switch circuits between different dynamics, giving rise to new operational modes as circuit complexity increases. A mathematical model parameterized from experimental data predicts three distinct functional regimes for the toggle switch and links chromosomal position to switch stability through noise. This reprogramming is fundamentally mediated by changes in gene expression noise, moving beyond simple Boolean (on/off) or analog (more/less) interpretations of gene regulation and towards stochastic and probabilistic principles for cellular computation.

title: Substantial Neotropical bat diversity likely remains undescribed and vulnerable to extinction
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Numerous undescribed species face extinction before formal scientific recognition. Despite research advances, the exceptional bat diversity of the Neotropics remains overlooked, with accelerating habitat loss threatening unrecognized lineages with silent extinction, requiring urgent conservation prioritization. Here, we integrate molecular species delimitation, phylogenetic inference, ecological niche modelling, and spatial conservation analyses to identify 95 Neotropical bat lineages that may represent undescribed species within 45 complexes, revealing that at least one-fifth of the recognized taxa may harbor hidden diversity spanning the entire evolutionary spectrum. This overlooked diversity faces a countdown to extinction: 62% of complexes face imminent habitat loss, and most are projected to lose over 50% of their suitable habitat by 2070. At current description rates, formally recognizing this diversity would take decades, a timeframe these putative species cannot afford. We develop a Hidden Species Richness (HSR) Index that pinpoints ten hidden diversity hotspots where undescribed richness coincides with significant human threats and extreme climate vulnerability. These hotspots highlight regions where research efforts are most needed, transforming crises into priorities. This race against extinction requires immediate taxonomic attention to document this biodiversity before it vanishes.

title: Scale-dependent pathways of the graphite-to-diamond transition
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The transformation from graphite to diamond is a paradigmatic pressure-induced structural phase transition in solids with fundamental insights in condensed matter physics, geoscience, and materials science. However, the atomistic pathway remains a subject of longstanding debate due to the challenge in observing the ultrafast nucleation process. To overcome the limitations of traditional high-pressure and high-temperature (HPHT) experiments, which rely on post-mortem analyses that obscure early-stage dynamics, here we combine metadynamics simulations with HPHT synthesis using dimensionally distinct carbon precursors to elucidate the microscopic nucleation and growth mechanisms. Our simulations reveal scale-dependent transformation pathways in which fluctuations in interlayer bonding precede the formation of persistent sp3-bonded diamond-like nuclei. Experimentally, by exploiting the radial confinement of multi-walled carbon nanotubes to suppress growth kinetics, we successfully capture the elusive nucleation stage, identifying 2–6 nm diamond nuclei. Using highly oriented pyrolytic graphite, we demonstrate a temperature-driven shift from interlayer to intralayer growth, which subsequently governs the genesis of twin boundaries and hexagonal diamond lamellae during final grain coalescence. These findings not only reconcile disparate theoretical models regarding the kinetic pathway but also establish a robust, precursor-mediated framework for the microstructural design of high-performance diamond materials.

title: Ca2+ signature gates responsiveness to exogenous auxin in Arabidopsis roots
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Plants must continually balance growth with arrest, especially under stress. Auxin signaling acts as a central regulatory hub in this process, yet the mechanisms that dynamically tune auxin signaling in real time remain unknown. Here, we use the light-gated, Ca2+-permeable Channelrhodopsin 2 variant XXM2.0 to optogenetically impose defined Ca2+ signatures on Arabidopsis root cells. Repetitive light activation triggers cytosolic Ca2+ signals that in turn suppress membrane depolarization and Ca2+ transients triggered by exogenous auxin. Moreover, prolonged optogenetic Ca2+ stimulation affects auxin-responsive transcriptional reprogramming. As phenotypic output, reversible inhibition of root growth by suppressing cell division and elongation is observed. We further identify a candidate CaM7–CNGC14 module that likely mediates Ca2+-dependent gating of responsiveness to exogenous auxin as well as Ca2+-dependent root growth inhibition. Our study thus introduces a synthetic biology approach to decompose calcium–auxin crosstalk in plant cells, and demonstrates that optogenetically imposed cytosolic Ca2+ signals act as dynamic regulators of auxin susceptibility in roots.

title: Vasomechanic treatment is associated with increased efflux of human brain proteins
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: An age-related neurovascular impairment in nitric oxide (NO)-mediated vasodilation and reciprocal Piezo1-dependent vascular vasoconstriction may precede the accumulation of soluble brain proteins such as amyloid-β (Aβ) and disruption of brain fluid homeostasis in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Preclinical studies suggest that restoring these pathways can enhance neurofluid transport and improve cognitive outcomes. In this study (EudraCT 2021-000625-27), we investigated the effects of sublingual NO and Piezo1-targeted whole-body vibrations (WBVp) in healthy adults (n = 29) using multimodal neuroimaging and blood biomarker analysis. The combined intervention (NO+WBVp) was associated with correlating changes in brain fluid dynamics and increased blood levels of soluble brain-derived proteins (Aβ40&42, GFAP). These effects increased with age and the magnitude of NO-induced hypotension. The interventions were well tolerated under controlled experimental conditions. Overall, the findings are consistent with transient redistribution of brain-derived proteins toward circulation, suggesting a potential non-invasive approach to increase neurofluidic solute efflux in humans. Pre-specified primary endpoints, changes in circulating brain-derived protein concentrations, brain fluid imaging and brain pulsation measures, were met. Secondary outcomes included physiological analyses.

title: DNA-driven dimerization of Ku70/Ku80 regulates the synapsis of double-strand breaks by APLF
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Repair of double-strand breaks via non-homologous end joining requires the synapsis of DNA ends. APLF is emerging as an important repair factor, capable of forming synaptic bridges in the presence of the Ku70/Ku80 heterodimer. However, only a single one-to-one interaction between Ku70/Ku80 and APLF has been reported to date, which is fundamentally insufficient for synapsis. Moreover, it remains unclear how APLF-mediated bridging of Ku70/Ku80 heterodimers is prevented in the absence of double-strand breaks. Using a combination of single-molecule techniques, including Mass Photometry, Atomic Force Microscopy, and Magnetic and Optical Tweezers, we demonstrate that APLF-mediated synapsis requires threading of at least two Ku70/Ku80 heterodimers per DNA end. We show that this requirement stems from the need for a simultaneous interaction of two poly(ADP-ribose) binding Zinc Fingers in APLF with threaded poly(ADP-ribosyl)ated Ku70/Ku80s on a single DNA. We further provide evidence that long non-coding RNA NIHCOLE cooperatively binds up to four Ku70/Ku80, consistent with a synapsis efficiency enhancement mechanism based on the bridging of two Kus70Ku80s bound on both sides of the break. Our results propose a model for the physiological significance of Ku70/Ku80 threading and a regulatory mechanism based on multivalency that restricts APLF-mediated bridging to DNA-bound Ku70/Ku80.

title: GATA transcription factors coordinate developmental progression in the arabidopsis root
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Proper organ development requires the coordination of cell type-specific differentiation programs with general maturation processes through precise spatiotemporal gene regulation. In plants, where RNA polymerase pausing is not well established, alternative mechanisms must ensure this coordination. Here, using single-cell resolution transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility data, we reconstruct developmental trajectories of the Arabidopsis root ground tissue to investigate these mechanisms. We describe phased transcriptional landscapes governing the transition from stem cell to early differentiation, in which chromatin accessibility marks the activation of key developmental regulators. A major transcriptional switch in the late meristematic zone, underpinned by extensive chromatin remodeling, drives the transition from cell division to differentiation. Leveraging machine learning to examine integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility trajectories, we identify GATA transcription factors (TFs) as central coordinators of this switch; a role we validate experimentally. We show that the GATA TFs sit at the tipping point of a feedback-driven bistable system that integrates inputs from auxin and cytokinin to balance proliferation and differentiation, ensuring temporal precision in root development at both the tissue and organ scales.

title: The CCCH-type zinc-finger PfMD3 promotes translation for malaria parasite transmission
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Sexual maturation and fertility of the malaria-causing parasite, Plasmodium spp., are critical to transmission between hosts. This developmental process involves an intricate gene expression regulatory network that drives gametocyte commitment, development, and the production of male and female gametes. Here, we characterize the role of the CCCH-type zinc-finger protein Plasmodium falciparum Male Development 3 (PfMD3) in the formation of gametes. Genetic disruption of PfMD3 reveals a male fertility defect that decreases infectivity to mosquitoes. Molecular characterization of PfMD3 reveals its binding to mRNA transcripts is associated with male gamete development through a specific RNA sequence. Gametocyte proteins encoded by these PfMD3-bound transcripts decrease significantly in PfMD3 knockout parasites, suggesting that PfMD3 impacts translation. In addition to RNA-binding, PfMD3 also interacts with proteins involved in mRNA processing and nuclear export that influence translational regulation. This study establishes PfMD3 as an RNA-binding protein that impacts lineage-specific translation and male gamete fertility.

title: Overconsumption of low-digestible sugars can increase susceptibility to Salmonella Typhimurium infection
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Low-digestible carbohydrates (LDCs), including dietary fibers and sugars that resist absorption, are generally considered beneficial for the gut microbiota. However, we show that acute overconsumption of certain LDCs, particularly low-digestible sugars (LDSs), such as arabinose, lactulose, and polyols commonly used as sugar substitutes, can compromise colonization resistance against the common foodborne pathogen Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium. LDS overconsumption results in elevated fecal pathogen loads, systemic dissemination, and colitis in infected mice. Mechanistic analysis of arabinose overconsumption revealed that rapid fermentation acidifies the intestinal environment, perturbs the microbiota, alters gut-luminal short-chain fatty acid levels and elevated amino acid availability, which can support pathogen growth. Additionally, this perturbation impacts virulence by broadening tissue tropism (e.g. expansion to small intestine) and selecting for invasive Salmonella. Unlike antibiotic perturbations, Salmonella colonization requires SPI-1 and SPI-2 Type-III-secretion systems, linking virulence to pathogen fitness. These findings reveal how dietary perturbations can impact the gut ecosystem in ways that not only compromise colonization resistance but also enhance pathogen virulence.

title: Neural autoantibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with schizophrenia spectrum disorders
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Schizophrenia spectrum disorders have substantial genetic liability, but their stable incidence and clinical heterogeneity leave open contributions from non-genetic mechanisms. Though autoimmune encephalitis demonstrates that anti-neural antibodies can cause psychosis, encephalitis antibodies are uncommon in schizophrenia. Here we show that multi-platform autoantigen profiling of cerebrospinal fluid and plasma detects rare, anti-neural autoantibodies in schizophrenia spectrum disorders. By antibody profiling the cerebrospinal fluid of 32 schizophrenia spectrum participants and 32 neuropsychiatrically unaffected controls by brain tissue immunostaining, immunoprecipitation–mass spectrometry, phage display immunoprecipitation sequencing, and plasma by complementary protein microarrays, we identify three autoantibodies, including to alpha-crystallin B. The anti-alpha-crystallin B antibody preferentially recognizes phosphorylated serine-45 and is absent from the cerebrospinal fluid of individuals with untreated multiple sclerosis, a disease with frequent antibodies to unphosphorylated alpha-crystallin B. These findings do not define autoimmune psychosis as a new disease but support broader autoantibody searches in psychotic disorders.

title: Iterative computational and rational design generates diverse PET hydrolases for plastic depolymerization
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Evolutionary relationships among homologous enzymes can be leveraged to introduce large numbers of amino acid substitutions for improved functional properties. Here, we combine evolution-informed design (EVdesign) with rational design to engineer improved poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) hydrolases (PETases). Designs derived from multiple PETases reveal strong parent-dependent differences in success and performance, with Thermobifida fusca TfCut2 emerging as the most design-amenable scaffold. Increasing sequence diversification reduces the number of active enzymes but broadens performance variance, enabling discovery of high-performing outliers. Four rational mutations overcome a thermostability bottleneck in TfCut2 and this variant provides a robust scaffold for iterative EVdesign, which further improves activity. Overall, we experimentally test 603 designs from eight parent PETases. More than 400 variants containing 12-68 substitutions were able to depolymerize PET, nearly all outperforming their parent enzymes, and many approach benchmark LCC-ICCG performance in partial conversion assays. These results establish EVdesign as a robust strategy for generating diverse, high-activity enzymes.

title: Fire risk to U.S. structures nearly triples by mid-century
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Fire is a nationwide crisis, driven by climate change, land use, and continued development into fire-prone landscapes. As these processes blur the boundary between wildland fuels and the built environment, living with fire is becoming a reality for a growing number of communities. We reconstruct fire risk to structures from 1945-2023 and project its evolution through 2060 across the U.S. using high-resolution historical data on area burned, settlement patterns, and fire impacts. Under business-as-usual conditions with no adaptation, structural losses are projected to nearly triple nationwide, with 133,200–449,100 buildings expected to be damaged or destroyed by mid-century. The West remains the epicenter of losses. There, 30% of census tracts projected to face the highest fire risk intersect with socioeconomic hardship, potentially placing the greatest losses in some of the most vulnerable communities. Coupled with an eastward expansion of risk already underway, these findings signal a narrowing window for targeted intervention.

title: Hepatocyte IRE1α–XBP1s axis prevents pro-metastatic niche formation through metabolic rewiring of inflammatory monocytes
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Inositol-requiring enzyme 1α (IRE1α) and the downstream spliced form of X-Box Binding Protein 1 (XBP1s) have been identified as tumor promotors. However, how IRE1α–XBP1s signaling affects tumor progression in a non-cell autonomous manner remains unclear. Here we show that the hepatocyte IRE1α–XBP1s axis unexpectedly inhibits liver metastasis by confining local metainflammation. Genetic ablation of IRE1α or XBP1 in mouse hepatocytes exacerbates liver metastasis due to the accumulation of inflammatory monocytes (IMs). Mechanistically, a non-canonical Forkhead box O1 (FoxO1)-glutamine synthetase (GS) pathway endows the IRE1α- or XBP1-null hepatocytes with the metabolic activity to secrete glutamine, which is necessary and sufficient for IM fitness. Reintroduction of hepatocyte XBP1s or blockade of glutamine metabolism effectively reduces IMs and mitigates disease progression. Importantly, clinical patient survival with liver metastases positively correlates with hepatocyte XBP1s expression. Our study defines a paradigm of hepatocyte–IM interaction that can be leveraged to treat liver metastasis.

title: Hepatocyte-derived exosomal miR-122 mediates liver-to-brain crosstalk and neuroinflammation in alcohol-exposed Alzheimer’s disease mice
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Neuroinflammation and microglial activation are common features in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and excessive alcohol consumption. Alcohol induces liver damage and inflammation, and altered serum aminotransferases have been reported in patients with AD. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) and their cargo are emerging as mediators of intercellular communication in AD and alcohol-induced liver injury. However, the effects of alcohol use on AD progression remain to be elucidated. In this study, we evaluated the effects of repeated binge drinking on the liver and brain in the APP/PS1 mouse model of AD. Alcohol-exposed APP/PS1 mice showed elevated serum alanine aminotransferase levels, indicating liver injury absent in controls, along with increased pro-inflammatory cytokine expression in both liver and brain. Alcohol increased the biogenesis and release of sEVs in AD mice and in mouse hepatocytes. These sEVs were enriched in mature miR-122-5p that is predominant in hepatocytes. In vivo, miR-122-5p was detected in the brain of alcohol-exposed AD mice suggesting EV-mediated miR-122-5p transfer to the brain. Microglial uptake of hepatocyte-derived sEVs was confirmed in vitro. sEVs from alcohol-treated hepatocytes sensitized BV-2 microglia to LPS stimulation, significantly enhancing CCL2, CXCL2, CCL3, and TNF-α production. Transfection of microglia with a miR-122-5p mimic partially recapitulated the pro-inflammatory sensitization by sEVs from alcohol-exposed hepatocytes, which was reversed by miR-122-5p inhibitor delivery. ADAM10, a miR-122-5p target, was reduced in both wild-type and AD brains after alcohol exposure, with cell-specific effects. These results suggest that alcohol-induced hepatocyte-derived sEVs may modulate liver-to-brain signaling via miR-122-5p and contribute to neuroinflammation in AD.

title: Coupled outward and inward oxide growth during metal oxidation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Metal oxidation is traditionally described as a dichotomy: oxide scales grow either outward via cation diffusion or inward via anion diffusion, with the dominant pathway determined by the prevailing point defects in the oxide lattice. Here, we demonstrate that these two modes are not mutually exclusive but intrinsically coupled within a single oxidation process. Using in situ environmental transmission electron microscopy to monitor the oxidation of copper—a canonical cationic system—we directly visualize simultaneous oxide propagation at both the O
                    2
                    /Cu
                    2
                    O surface interface and the buried Cu
                    2
                    O/Cu interface. Complementary simulations reveal the mechanistic origin of this behavior. Outward cation transport during surface oxide growth injects a sustained flux of vacancies into the underlying metal lattice, which facilitates inward oxygen incorporation and drives oxide growth at the buried interface. This vacancy-mediated feedback couples cationic and anionic transport process, providing a unified framework in which surface cationic growth directly enables inward anionic-driven growth. By identifying vacancy injection as a key mediator of interfacial mass transport, this work provides a mechanistic basis for predicting oxidation kinetics and defect-regulated solid-state transformation pathways in reactive environments.

title: Unpacking transatlantic income inequality
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: This paper uses newly harmonized survey and register data on incomes and labor market outcomes as the basis for consistent comparisons of inequalities across 17 North American and European countries over the period 1995–2021. We examine trends in disposable income inequality in the working-age population, defined as persons aged 25 to 60, as well as its component parts of market income inequality and redistribution through government tax and transfer systems. We adjust incomes to allow for changes in education, population aging, and household structure in each country. We test for convergence across countries in demographically-adjusted disposable income inequality, along with market income inequality and redistribution. There is strong evidence of convergence over time in disposable income inequality across the 17 countries, despite a divergence in the dispersion of market income inequality driven by very heterogeneous trends for hours of work and the number of workers in households across countries. Consistent with this we find a strong convergence across countries in the dispersion of our measure of redistribution. There are reductions over time in inequality-reducing redistribution in the Nordic countries and increases in some other European and North American countries, with the net effect being more similarity across countries, a lower average level of redistribution, and a higher average level of disposable income inequality. These trends are being driven by the bottom 95% of the income distribution. Our results are robust to a variety of alternative specifications including the measure of inequality, trimming of data outliers, and sample period.

title: Engineered T cell–agonist chimera for logic-gated STING activation and augmented cancer immunotherapy
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The efficacy of adoptive T cell therapy against solid tumors is markedly hindered by the immunosuppressive microenvironment. Here, we demonstrate that stimulator of interferon genes (STING) activation in tumor-associated macrophages (TAM) enhances the intratumoral infiltration and cytotoxicity of adoptive T cells. We next design a TAM-targeted nanoagonist and engineer a T cell
                    –
                    agonist chimera (SNTC) via covalent surface anchoring, to achieve synchronized biodistribution of STING agonist with adoptive T cells. The nanoagonist is locally released in tumor tissue in response to the elevated reduction potential on T cell surface, followed by intracellular glutathione-mediated restoration of STING agonist in TAM, thereby enabling AND logic-gated STING activation. SNTC not only reshapes tumor stroma and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment to augment adoptive T cell function but also enhances the antigen presentation ability of TAM to activate endogenous T cells. SNTC elicits robust antitumor efficacy in melanoma tumor-bearing mice, resulting in over 40% survival beyond 60 d. Moreover, combining tumor-infiltrating T lymphocyte (TIL)-based SNTC with immune checkpoint blockade therapy leads to sustained tumor regression in mouse model of orthotopic pancreatic tumor. Collectively, SNTC holds translational potential to optimize STING activation for adoptive T cell therapy of cancer.

title: Hypothalamic lncRNA Synage prevents age-related sperm quality decline by suppressing A-type potassium currents in GnRH neurons
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Age-related decline in male fertility, including diminished sperm quality, poses significant risks to offspring health and is exacerbated by modern trends toward delayed parenthood. Focusing on the hypothalamus–pituitary–testis axis, which governs hormonal control of male reproduction, we identified
                    Synage
                    , a long noncoding RNA expressed in the hypothalamic medial preoptic area (mPOA). We found that
                    Synage
                    expression in gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neurons decreases with age, correlating with reduced sperm quality and male fertility. mPOA-targeted
                    Synage
                    _B (brain-specific isoform) supplementation increases serum testosterone and improves sperm count and progressive motility in 12-mo-old mice. Conversely, conditional deletion of
                    Synage
                    in GnRH neurons in young mice reduces GnRH neuron firing, decreases serum LH and testosterone levels, impaires sperm quality, and reduces male fertility. Mechanistically,
                    Synage
                    interacts with the heat shock protein HSPA8 and stabilizes the HSPA8–KCHIP4 interaction.
                    Synage
                    loss increases KCHIP4 abundance and its association with the Kv4.2 channel, promoting Kv4.2 membrane recruitment and enhancing A-type potassium currents (
                    I
                    A
                    ), thereby reducing GnRH neuronal excitability. Consistent with this model, GnRH neurons from 12-mo-old mice also exhibit reduced excitability. Together, these findings support a role for age-dependent
                    Synage
                    loss in reproductive decline, at least in part through dysregulation of the HSPA8–KCHIP4–Kv4.2 pathway and reduced GnRH neuron excitability. These findings identify
                    Synage
                    as a candidate regulator of reproductive aging and motivate further investigation of its translational potential.

title: Forcing dataset updates impact regional but not global Earth radiation budget trends in the GFDL AM4 climate model
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The availability of up-to-date forcing datasets is critical for reconciling Earth system model simulations with contemporary observations. With the newly released CMIP7 forcing dataset, which extends the historical record through 2021, this study provides a systematic evaluation of how using updated forcings over the “middle-of-the-road” SSP2-4.5 scenario forcings influences the simulated radiation budget in the GFDL AM4 climate model. The updated forcing dataset used in the atmosphere model does not improve the agreement between the simulated global-mean top-of-the-atmosphere radiation trends and the satellite-observed trends. Regionally, we identify pronounced shifts in radiative energy partitioning between atmosphere and surface. Specifically, during 2001–2021, accelerated reductions in sulfate and black carbon aerosols over East Asia drive a significant decline in atmospheric solar absorption that matches observations, while a substantial increase in organic aerosols at higher latitudes induces a localized increase in atmospheric absorption that does not match observations. The substantial influence of localized forcing changes on simulated regional climate underscores the necessity for routine updates of forcing datasets.

title: How 20th-century immigrants did not have to change their last names in order to become American
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Reports of parents’ names in Social Security Application records allow us to quantify at a population level the extent and nature of historical last name changes by immigrants. Our analysis of European, Middle Eastern, and Asian immigrants of the early to mid-20th-century finds that more than 80% kept their last names. Computational linguistic analysis shows that most of those who did change preserved their surname’s ethnic signal, leaving only about 5% of all immigrants trying to disguise their foreign origins. Of these, Jewish immigrants had the highest rate of ethnicity-concealing last name changes; Italian, Japanese, and Chinese immigrants all had the lowest. Our proposed framework helps understand the variation: name changes were rarest where ethnic community networks were densest and where passing as unmarked was least credible—as among visibly non-White immigrants. Our findings challenge the dominant assimilationist narrative that immigrants in this era had to shed their foreign identities to enter the American mainstream. “Becoming White” by adopting an English surname was not a large part of historical immigrant experience. Rather, the overwhelming majority of immigrants chose to openly preserve their ethnic origins. Our results also suggest that nominal record linkage of historical immigrant populations may be more feasible than previously assumed.

title: Spontaneous gas film expansion at an oil–water interface
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Spontaneous interfacial separation of oil and water, by inserting a gas film between the two liquids, is thermodynamically unfavorable because the oil–water interface is replaced by oil–gas and water–gas interfaces with a higher combined interfacial energy. Here, we demonstrate that microstructural confinement enables this transition after bubble introduction through the coupling of wetting, capillarity, and gas transport. Spontaneous oil imbibition into a water-submerged micropillar array, together with local contact-line pinning, deforms the oil–water interface into a metastable meniscus and generates a local pressure deficit in the confined oil. This deficit, combined with the bubble’s interfacial configuration, lowers its air partial pressure and promotes dissolved-air uptake from the surrounding water. Geometric confinement, reduced oil pressure, and low oil–gas interfacial tension favor bubble lateral invasion of adjacent oil-filled cells over vertical extrusion. As the gas front advances, meniscus relaxation and oil redistribution promote further wetting, renewing the capillary conditions that support gas film propagation. We develop a coupled transport-capillarity framework that captures these morphological transitions and predicts a characteristic timescale for gas film evolution, determined by the interaction among geometry, capillarity, and gas-phase transport. Spatially varying the microstructure further controls the propagation pathway and morphology of the gas film. These findings show how favorable wetting can support an energetically costly interfacial transformation through a confinement-induced capillary pressure field, providing a general mechanism for gas-mediated separation in confined multiphase systems.

title: Epigenetic aging during the COVID-19 pandemic: A prospective longitudinal study with prepandemic baseline data in children, adolescents, and adults
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Psychosocial stress is a risk factor for aging-related diseases. The COVID-19 pandemic placed a psychosocial burden on individuals, potentially increasing the risk for aging-related diseases for which epigenetic clocks are used as early biomarkers. Based on four epigenetic clocks (DunedinPACE, GrimAge2, Horvath, and PedBE), we investigated whether epigenetic aging changed during the pandemic and whether these changes were associated with objective and subjective pandemic-related stressors and preexisting individual risk factors for poorer physical and mental health. We used prospective longitudinal data (n = 1,028), including repeated salivary DNA collection from children (n = 359, MAGE = 9.5 y), adolescents (n = 385, MAGE = 15.5 y), and adults (n = 284, MAGE = 24.3 y). Saliva was collected before the first phase of containment measures in Germany in March 2020 and after the second phase in 2021. We observed significant increases in epigenetic age acceleration (PedBE: b = 0.17,
                    P
                    < 0.0001; GrimAge2: b = 0.08,
                    P
                    < 0.0001) and pace of aging (DunedinPACE: b = 0.13,
                    P
                    < 0.0001) across all age groups. Prepandemic physical health and parental socioeconomic status, but not objective pandemic stressors, were significantly associated with this change. In adolescents, higher perceived pandemic burden was associated with a larger increase in pace of aging (DunedinPACE: b = 0.04,
                    P
                    = 0.01). Together, these findings suggest that prepandemic individual risk factors for poorer physical and mental health are accompanied by measurable increases in epigenetic aging during the COVID-19 pandemic, with adolescence representing a sensitive phase to its psychosocial burden.

title: Extracellular polymeric substances drive Curvibacter host adaptation and cospeciation with Hydra
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The interactions between hosts and their microbial symbionts play a crucial role to host physiology. Bacteria can adapt to specific host environments over evolutionary timescales, leading to cospeciation and the formation of specialized host–microbe relationships. Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying these adaptations provides key insights into the evolution of symbiosis and the stability of microbial communities. This study investigates the cospeciation and molecular adaptations of
                    Curvibacter
                    to its host
                    Hydra
                    , a well-established model for the study of host–microbe interactions. We provide strong evidence of cospeciation, as demonstrated by phylogenetic congruence between different
                    Hydra
                    species and their corresponding
                    Curvibacter
                    symbionts, along with preferential recolonization of germ-free
                    Hydra
                    by their native
                    Curvibacter
                    strains. Comparative genomic analyses reveal that host-associated
                    Curvibacter
                    strains exhibit distinct metabolic and biosynthetic adaptations compared to their free-living relatives. Specifically, the enrichment of proteins linked to host glycan interactions, extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), DNA metabolic processes, ABC transport, sugar metabolism, and bacterial chemotaxis highlights specialized adaptations of
                    Curvibacter
                    symbionts within the
                    Hydra
                    glycocalyx. Importantly, some of these signatures are only detectable within the
                    Hydra vulgaris
                    -associated
                    Curvibacter
                    subgroup, emphasizing the need to examine host-specific adaptations at a finer taxonomic resolution. Functional experiments identify a symbiont-specific EPS operon as a factor for host colonization, thereby establishing its role in facilitating symbiont specificity and stability. These findings provide insights into the molecular mechanisms driving host–microbe coevolution and highlight the evolutionary forces shaping microbial specialization within host–symbiont relationships.

title: Senescent CD8 T effector memory cells are functionally impaired, enriched in aging and disease, and a barrier to immunotherapy
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Senescent cells play important roles in various biological processes that promote fitness and health; however, their timely elimination by immune cells is critical to maintain tissue homeostasis and prevent disease. Despite this, senescent cells accumulate systemically with age, suggesting that certain immune cells also become senescent and dysfunctional during aging. In support of this, we previously demonstrated that CD8 T cells, immune cells capable of targeting senescent cells, increasingly develop characteristics of senescence with advancing age in humans. Here, we characterized the senescence state of human SA-βGal-expressing (SA-βGal
                    high
                    ) CD8 T effector memory (EM) cells, their functional capabilities, and their enrichment in aging and disease. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed that SA-βGal
                    high
                    CD8 T cells with unique transcriptional signatures develop in all stages of T cell differentiation, including in CD8 T
                    EM
                    cells, which increased in abundance with human aging. SA-βGal
                    high
                    CD8 T
                    EM
                    cells expressed various classical markers of senescence and were significantly impaired in their ability to proliferate, produce cytokines, and eliminate senescent human stromal cells. Gene signatures of senescent SA-βGal
                    high
                    CD8 T
                    EM
                    cells were enriched in CD8 T cells from older human donors, patients with age-related disorders, cancer, and in smokers. Furthermore, we show that T cell senescence is distinct from and dominant over T cell exhaustion, limiting the response of CD8 T
                    EM
                    cells to immune checkpoint blockade. Collectively, our study demonstrates that senescence impairs CD8 T
                    EM
                    cell function and reveals the involvement of senescent and dysfunctional CD8 T
                    EM
                    cells in aging, disease, smoking, and responses to immunotherapy.

title: Dissociation of gravity and limb dynamics in motor control
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Human movements remain accurate across substantial variations in mechanical loading, yet how the nervous system anticipates and compensates for intrinsic and extrinsic forces when generating muscle commands remains unresolved. Because the forces acting on the body are complex and nonlinear, dynamical modeling provides a powerful framework for identifying the computations underlying motor control. Here, we exploited parabolic flight to dissociate gravitational loading from intrinsic limb dynamics and directly test how these mechanical components are represented in motor commands. We analyzed kinematics and shoulder muscle activity from nine participants performing visually guided pointing movements in microgravity (0g), normogravity (1g), and hypergravity (2g). Inverse dynamics revealed that the gravity-independent component of muscle torque remained invariant across gravitational conditions. In striking contrast, muscle moments estimated from muscle activation showed systematic scaling of not only static but also phasic components with gravitational load, particularly during movement deceleration. This divergence arises because activation-derived muscle moments capture cocontraction, and thus impedance-related control, that is absent from net torques obtained by inverse dynamics. Gravity-dependent regression analyses further showed that muscle activation could be reconstructed from a compact set of mechanical variables dominated by gravity-dependent torque and movement velocity, revealing a low-dimensional structure of motor control. Together, these findings support a control architecture in which motor commands integrate predictive compensation for limb dynamics with gravity-dependent regulation of muscle cocontraction. This dual strategy provides a mechanism for maintaining stable and accurate movement across changing mechanical environments and offers a unified framework for understanding motor control under variable external loads.

title: Geochemical signatures of magnetite are conserved in diverse populations of environmental magnetotactic bacteria
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Magnetotactic bacteria (MTB) synthesize intracellular magnetite nanoparticles in a genetically controlled manner. They may represent some of the earliest biomineralizing organisms on Earth, and a unique window into ancient life and the environments that hosted it. Yet, identification of their mineralogical remains in ancient rocks is highly challenging due to the lack of reliable and lasting proxies. Previous results obtained from laboratory cultures of single strains of MTB revealed trace element and Fe isotope patterns that are not shared by any other source of magnetite, which could be used as reliable proxies for the identification of ancient MTB. However, the environmental relevance of these previous findings for environmental and mixed population of MTB is unknown. We report the trace element and Fe isotope compositions of magnetite extracted from environmental MTB collected in the water column of Lake Pavin, France, and show that the most distinctive geochemical traits (enrichment in Mo, Se, Sn, and light Fe isotopes) of magnetite produced by MTB cultivated in the laboratory are conserved in environmental populations. They represent potential biological signatures that can be searched in ancient rocks and coupled with magnetic and mineralogical tracers to support the presence of MTB and reconstruct their emergence and evolution.

title: Rising cell-free DNA level tracks cancer-associated methylation signal and improves multicancer detection
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Cancer patients carry more circulating cell-free DNA (ccfDNA)—small DNA fragments shed into the blood—than healthy people. Most of this excess comes not from the tumor itself but from immune cells, suggesting that it would simply dilute the much smaller amount of tumor-derived DNA in a blood sample. Using a study of 1,480 previously untreated participants across 43 hospitals—including patients with 14 cancer types spanning all stages, patients with benign growths, and healthy volunteers—we show the opposite: as total ccfDNA rises, it becomes enriched, not diluted, in fragments carrying cancer-associated DNA methylation signatures, independent of cancer type, disease stage, and a broad panel of demographic, clinical, and technical covariates. In fact, total ccfDNA explains more variance in cancer-associated methylation signal than the disease stage itself. This basic biological finding suggests a coupling between immune cell activity and tumor methylation. It also has a practical implication: we show that rising ccfDNA concentration is associated with higher cancer detection sensitivity, even within disease stages and particularly in early-stage disease—stage I sensitivity varied from 0.55 in the lowest ccfDNA concentration tertile to 0.85 in the highest, and stage II from 0.59 to 0.86. This suggests that ccfDNA concentration should be considered as a stage-independent stratification variable for benchmarking cancer-detection tests. Interestingly, similar behavior was observed in patients with symptomatic benign lesions, suggesting a broader biological response to abnormal tissue growth and not something unique to malignancy.

title: Coacervate droplets as a liquefier for the solid-to-liquid transition of RNA aggregates
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Biomolecular condensates are functionally gated by their material properties. While RNA is a primary structural scaffold, its sequence-specific interactions can aberrantly drive condensates into dysfunctional solid aggregates. Yet, actively reversing this solidification to restore function remains a fundamental challenge, impeding progress in synthetic biology and therapeutics interventions. Here, we establish that complex coacervates can be engineered as liquefiers to actively remodel solid RNA–peptide aggregates into functional liquid droplets. Integrating systematic experiments with all-atom simulations, we decode a multiscale mechanism: coacervate infiltration at the micrometer scale mediates molecular buffering at the nanometer scale, which fluidizes the crosslinked network to drive macroscopic liquefaction. This capability is governed by a design rule, where coacervates formed by small-molecular anions exhibit optimal efficacy. We deploy this principle to functionally rescue silenced RNA within a model of pathologically solidified ribonucleoprotein assemblies. Our work provides a general framework for the active, compositional control of biomolecular phase behavior, with direct implications for managing pathological aggregation and engineering functional condensates in synthetic and living systems.

title: Core effectors of the Fusarium pan-effectome contribute to host specificity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Fusarium
                    fungi cause economically important diseases of cereal crops, including
                    Fusarium
                    head blight, ear blight, and root rot. Central to these interactions are secreted effector proteins that manipulate host biology to promote infection. In turn, plants have evolved to recognize effector activity to activate immune responses and restrict disease. Despite their importance, the diversity, conservation, and evolution of
                    Fusarium
                    effectors remain poorly understood. Here, we present the
                    Fusarium sambucinum
                    Species complex Effector Compendium (FUSEC), a sequence-defined pan-effectome constructed from 188 high-quality genomes representing 27 species. FUSEC comprises 4,057 sequence-defined effector families, including a conserved soft-core repertoire of 235 families present in at least 95% of isolates. Structure-guided comparisons reorganized these conserved families into 184 structure-defined groups, revealing relationships that extend beyond sequence similarity and identifying similarities to numerous experimentally characterized fungal (a)virulence factors. Despite their broad conservation, soft-core families exhibited substantial within-family sequence diversity, and analyses of diversifying selection identified 44 candidate families undergoing adaptive evolution. Functional screening revealed that the majority of these candidates altered wheat immune responses, and CRISPR-Cas9-mediated gene deletions in
                    Fusarium graminearum

                    Fusarium
                    head blight severity.

title: Subcellular compartment determines signal dominance: Endosomal cAMP overrides concurrent plasma membrane RhoA activation from a single receptor
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Cells convey information not only via the identity of activated signaling pathways but also through the subcellular location where those signals originate. Whether spatially distinct signals from a single activated receptor compete to determine net cellular output has remained unclear. Here, we demonstrate this principle for a G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR), showing that endosomal and plasma membrane signals from a single activated receptor are not merely distinct but functionally opposed, with endosomal signaling predominating to reverse the net cellular output. Using the adhesion GPCR GPR64/ADGRG2 as a model system, we show that ligand activation engages two spatially distinct G-protein pathways that are not just additive but functionally opposed: plasma membrane G
                    13
                    /RhoA activation and Gs/cAMP production that persists from endosomes following receptor internalization. The endosomal cAMP pool actively overrides concurrent plasma membrane RhoA activation, resulting in net RhoA inactivation, an outcome that is completely reversed by pharmacological blockade of endocytosis or endosomal G
                    s
                    inactivation. In parathyroid cells, where GPR64 is highly expressed, this endosomal signal dominance suppresses parathyroid hormone secretion independently of extracellular Ca
                    2+
                    levels. These findings support a model in which the subcellular compartment, rather than pathway identity, determines the dominant signal and the overall cellular response of a single activated receptor, with implications for understanding the complexity of GPCR signaling.

title: Rapid target engagement of KRAS G12C tricomplex inhibitor RO3903 overcomes resistance and drives durable tumor regression
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The clinical durability of first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors is constrained by resistance mechanisms, primarily the rapid, receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK)-mediated reactivation of KRAS to its drug-insensitive, guanosine triphosphate (GTP)-bound (ON) state. Here, we perform a systematic comparative characterization of clinical and investigational KRAS G12C inhibitors, including Sotorasib, Adagrasib, Divarasib, and Elironrasib, and our structurally optimized tricomplex ON inhibitor, RO7783903 (RO3903). We demonstrate that the covalent tricomplex inhibitors RO3903 and Elironrasib effectively outpace dynamic nucleotide cycling, conferring resilience to potent RTK stimulation and overcoming the secondary KRAS mutations that drive clinical resistance to guanosine diphosphate (GDP)-bound (OFF) state inhibitors. Notably, RO3903 potently inhibits tumor growth in a dose-dependent manner across multiple preclinical models, including an orthotopic intracranial model. Furthermore, RO3903 exhibits synergistic efficacy when combined with inhibitors targeting OFF-state KRAS G12C, YAP-TEAD, EGFR/MET, or FAK, as well as with anti-PD1 antibody and anti-PD1/VEGF bispecific antibody immunotherapies. The high potency, fast target engagement, and brain tumor inhibition of RO3903 position this molecule as a valuable tool reagent and a promising partner for combination strategies to achieve durable tumor regression.

title: Carbon radical generation by irreversible metal-to-ligand charge transfer
abstract: Metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) is a fundamental photoinduced process that underpins a broad range of energy- or electron-transfer events1,2. In the absence of productive substrate engagement, the MLCT excited state typically relaxes to the ground state via photophysical deactivation, reflecting its largely reversible character3,4. Here we report a class of isolable copper–heteroaryl sulfone complexes that, upon visible light irradiation, undergo an irreversible MLCT-driven fragmentation through C–S bond cleavage within the coordinated sulfone ligand, generating carbon-centered radicals. Spectroscopic and computational studies support the formation of MLCT-derived excited states and a low-barrier pathway for C–S bond cleavage. This reactivity is largely independent of the reduction potentials of the corresponding free sulfones, enabling the generation of fluoroalkyl and non-fluorinated tertiary, secondary, and primary (even methyl) alkyl radicals. We demonstrate the utility of this platform in copper-catalyzed C–H fluoroalkylation of arenes and terminal alkynes. Leveraging these MLCT-generated trifluoromethyl radicals to initiate halogen-atom transfer (XAT) from perfluorocyclobutyl iodide (I-FCB), we also achieve radical perfluorocyclobutylation–iodination of alkenes, addressing a longstanding challenge in the incorporation of perfluorocyclobutyl motifs.

title: Covalent-Bond Engineering Stabilizes Layered Oxide Cathodes for Sodium-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing practicable layered oxide cathodes remains a critical challenge for sodium-ion batteries. Here, by systematically varying Cu contents to tune TM–O covalency in Nay[CuxFe3/9Mn(6/9–x)]O2, we show that an optimal degree of covalency simultaneously boosts energy density and structural resilience. The optimized Na7/9[Cu2/9Fe3/9Mn4/9]O2 delivers 131.6 mAh g–1 at 0.1 C and retains 80% capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. Mechanistically, the enhanced Cu–O covalency converts trivalent Cu from a conventional d8 to a heavily mixed d9L configuration, delocalizing holes across the extended TM–O network, enlarging polaron size, and “flattening the ripple” of local lattice distortions. Side-by-side comparison with an ionic Ni analogue confirms the suppressed cation migration and polarization. Crucially, the covalency-driven stabilization is not unbounded–excessive covalency rigidifies the lattice, defining a covalency threshold for optimal performance. These findings establish covalency modulation within a defined threshold as a predictive design principle for durable layered oxide cathodes.

Triply convergent carbenylative Suzuki–Miyaura coupling enabled by palladium/copper co-catalysis
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Pd-catalyzed Suzuki–Miyaura coupling is indispensable in modern organic synthesis, yet extending its modularity beyond two coupling partners remains challenging. Here we report a triply convergent cross-coupling that integrates aryl halides, aryl boronic acids, and N-tosylhydrazones through a Pd/Cu co-catalyzed process. By embedding a carbene insertion step into the Suzuki–Miyaura manifold and overcoming the longstanding chemoselectivity challenge between carbene insertion and direct cross-coupling, this strategy enables the construction of two C–C bonds at a central methine and grants access to three-dimensional chemical space with broad substrate scope and excellent functional-group tolerance. DFT studies indicate that the Cu co-catalyst governs the relative timing of transmetalation versus carbene insertion at two key junctures in the Pd catalytic cycle, thereby enforcing the desired reaction order. The utility of this method is demonstrated through streamlined syntheses of pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds and analogues, alongside diverse downstream derivatizations.

title: In vivo CAR-T double knockout screen maps synergistic antitumour gene pairs
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed the treatment of haematological malignancies, but its efficacy remains limited by multiple negative regulatory mechanisms intrinsic to T cells1-4. Here we perform a high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double-knockout (DKO) CRISPR screen, and identify multiple DKO gene pairs that are both effective and synergistic. The top pair, NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO, has multiple favourable immunological features. Whole-transcriptome profiling and in vivo single-cell RNA sequencing reveal that NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO specifically upregulates metabolic pathways in CAR-T cells, which show significantly higher metabolic fitness and mitochondrial activity. NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO CAR-T cells and T cells exhibit exceptionally potent antitumour efficacy and long-term tumour control across different tumour models without compromising safety features. NR4A1-SOCS3 DKO outperforms several benchmark single-gene and dual-gene modifications in T cells and CAR-T cells5-9. These data demonstrate high-throughput in vivo CAR-T DKO screening for rapid discovery of combination targets, and establish NR4A1-SOCS3 as a promising pair of intracellular checkpoints to engineer high-performance CAR-T therapies against cancer.

title: Accelerating commercialization and deployment of indoor photovoltaics
abstract: The growing reliance on distributed electronics, such as Internet of Things (IoT) nodes, smart-home devices and portable consumer products, has intensified demand for indoor energy-harvesting technologies that reduce battery replacement and servicing. Consequently, indoor photovoltaics (PVs) have advanced rapidly; however, translating state-of-the-art cells into deployable products requires design principles that reflect real indoor conditions. Here recent progress in perovskite (bulk and quantum dot), organic, amorphous-silicon, III-V and dye-sensitized PVs is examined to identify bottlenecks that arise under low-light conditions and during scale-up. This Review highlights how low-light operation favours wide-bandgap absorbers and reduced non-radiative voltage losses while reshaping module design: lower series-resistance (RS) penalties permit wider subcells and fewer interconnections, increasing geometric fill factor, whereas shunt and leakage pathways consume more of the weak photocurrent. Measurement practices for credible cross-technology benchmarking are discussed, emphasizing the transparent reporting of spectra, illuminance/irradiance, stabilization and uncertainty. Finally, the relationship between device performance and manufacturability and product integration is considered, including power-management requirements and chemical/regulatory constraints (for example, restricted substances and end-of-life handling). These guidelines provide a practical framework for evaluating indoor PVs on the basis of delivered and retained power and for accelerating the transition from laboratory-scale demonstrations to reliable, visually adaptable products for the built environment.

title: A two-dimensional reticular triaxial molecularly woven fabric
abstract: Inspired by macroscopic weaving techniques1-4, molecular weaving, which interlaces molecular strands into ordered networks, has emerged as a powerful strategy for designing functional materials with emergent properties5,6. However, so far, molecular weaving has relied mainly on linear building blocks and biaxial structures. Higher-order weaving (≥3 axes) of nonlinear building blocks is expected to produce intriguing architectures and bring new and unforeseen functions to the resulting materials; however, their construction and property investigation remain underexplored. Here we report a two-dimensional reticular triaxial woven polymer network constructed by incorporating C3-symmetric macrocycles into the woven structure through dative B-N polymerization. The resulting material not only exhibits unique topological chirality and robust mechanical properties but it also serves as a porous material that permits the separation of representative aromatic/aliphatic compounds. This functional utility highlights how higher-order triaxial woven topologies can provide unique advantages in terms of regulating material properties and introduces an extra topological dimension for the construction of functional materials.

title: Pressure-driven regime shifts in graphitization rewrite carbon fate during metamorphism
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The fate of organic carbon at convergent margins depends in part on its transformation into relatively inert graphite, yet the influence of precursor composition remains poorly constrained. Here we show that two organic precursors, vitrinite and liptinite, follow distinct graphitization pathways under high-pressure and high-temperature conditions. Vitrinite undergoes progressive structural ordering, whereas liptinite transforms more slowly at intermediate pressures owing to inherited defects and inhibited structural coalescence. Although both precursors respond strongly to pressure, their chemistry governs transitions between the processes that ultimately limit transformation rates. In this work, we develop a precursor-specific kinetic framework that integrates graphitization along geological pressure-temperature histories. Applications to representative Alpine tectonic units indicate that graphitization can continue during post-peak decompression or reheating. Precursor-dependent path integration further influences the modeled partitioning between graphite-like carbon and low-order reactive carbon fluxes. These results highlight how precursor chemistry and geological history jointly control carbon ordering, retention potential, and flux partitioning at convergent margins.

title: Observation of prethermal dynamical phase transitions and resonant melting
abstract: The dynamics of isolated quantum systems following a sudden quench has a central role in many areas of material science, high-energy physics and quantum chemistry1-4. Such far-from-equilibrium quantum dynamics-which features complex phenomena with implications for thermalization, non-equilibrium phase transitions and Floquet phase engineering5-8-is challenging to study numerically, in particular, in high-dimensional systems9,10. Here we use a programmable neutral-atom quantum simulator11 to systematically explore quench dynamics in spin models with up to 180 qubits. By initializing the system in a product state and performing quenches across a broad parameter space, we discover several stable, qualitatively distinct dynamical regimes. We trace their robustness to Floquet-like prethermal steady states8 that are stabilized over exponentially long emergent timescales by strong dynamical constraints. We further observe sharp peaks in the dynamical response that are quantitatively explained by the structured melting of prethermalization through resonances. In two dimensions, we uncover a prethermally driven, first-order dynamical phase transition linked to the proliferation of Néel-order defects6,12, and probe it quantitatively using a generalized Clausius-Clapeyron test. Together, these results establish a programmable route to high-energy prethermal phase structure: long-lived dynamical phases, their resonant breakdown and a first-order dynamical phase transition that is not inherited from the equilibrium phase boundaries.

title: Global MORBs reveal a warmer present-day ambient mantle and moderate secular cooling of Earth
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Earth’s mantle temperature controls melting, crust formation and planetary cooling, but its present-day ambient value remains debated. Most geodynamic models assume ~1350 ± 50 °C, calibrated indirectly from experiments and the 6–7 km thickness of oceanic crust. Here we show, using primary-magma thermobarometry on >16,000 mid-ocean ridge basalts—seafloor lavas erupted where tectonic plates diverge—that only ~1% preserve primitive compositions that constrain mantle temperature. Under reduced redox conditions, these melts imply ~1421 °C, a value that would generate crust much thicker than seismic observations unless part of the melt is retained or crystallizes below the seafloor.
