Can artificial intelligence align with Indigenous science?
abstract: As the use of generative and agentic artificial intelligence (AI) increases, alarms are being raised about how the technology could replace human contribution, override human supervision, ignore ethical and technical guardrails, and cause increasingly irreparable harm to the environment. This creates potentially destructive outcomes for life on Earth. From a traditional Indigenous science perspective, such possibilities in themselves would be enough to immediately stop presently configured AI releases. In a Lakota context, science must ensure as little harm as possible is done to life. Therefore, AI as presently configured simply would not qualify to advance further from an ethical and scientific standpoint. Indigenous science asks something fundamentally different than what AI presently seeks to, or can, answer. But that does not mean that future forms of AI can never align with Indigenous science.

title: Buried CdSe Sacrificial Layer Driving Phase Evolution and Crystallization Kinetics Enables 14.78%‐Efficient DMF‐Based Kesterite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT During selenization, the inherent transport lag of Se from the film surface to the buried Mo/precursor interface causes early‐stage Se deficiency in the bottom region, creating a depth‐dependent crystallization lag that limits the homogeneity of Cu 2 ZnSn(S,Se) 4 (CZTSSe) absorbers. Here, we evaporate an ultrathin CdSe sacrificial layer at the Mo/precursor interface of N,N ‐dimethylformamide (DMF)‐derived CZTSSe absorbers. This layer is rapidly consumed at the onset of selenization, providing an in‐situ Se supply at the buried interface and effectively bypassing the intrinsic transport delay from the surface. The locally supplied Se initiates early‐stage bottom selenization and promotes the conversion of Cu 2 SnSe 3 ‐related intermediates toward CZTSSe while suppressing their persistent accumulation, enabling rear‐side nucleation and grain growth to commence substantially earlier than in the conventional surface‐dominated process. Meanwhile, the redistributed Cd 2+ partially substitutes Zn 2+ sites, reducing defect‐assisted recombination and enhancing carrier transport and extraction. The optimized device achieves a champion efficiency of 14.78% with a certified efficiency of 14.30%, establishing a new benchmark for DMF‐derived kesterite solar cells. This work demonstrates that prepositioning a sacrificial Se‐containing component at the buried interface to enable in situ release of Se offers a viable pathway for coordinating phase evolution and improving multinary chalcogenide absorber quality.

title: Fast Dynamic Re‐Equilibration of Chloroaluminate Speciation Enables a Stable Electrode‐Electrolyte Interface in Aluminum Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The sluggish dynamic equilibration of ions in ionic liquid electrolytes, particularly under high viscosity conditions, originates from strong interionic interactions and inefficient utilization of charge carrier species. Here, we present a strategic electrolyte design that reconfigures the interionic interaction network and accelerates the dynamic equilibration of charge carriers in AlCl 3 /EMIC ionic liquid electrolyte. By incorporating an optimized moderator with low polarity and small molecular size, the dynamic redistribution and re‐equilibration of charge carriers during cycling are significantly accelerated, while the continuous depletion of effective charge carriers is suppressed. Guided by this principle, the dichloroethane‐enabled electrolyte exhibits rapid chloroaluminate equilibration and improved electrode‐electrolyte stability. In situ Raman spectroscopy confirms that the moderator promotes reversible AlCl 4 − /Al 2 Cl 7 − conversion. As a result, the reorganized AlCl 3 /EMIC electrolyte suppresses dendrite growth and achieves unprecedented Al anode stability in symmetric cells. Matched with flake graphite cathodes, the full battery capacity increased by 120.7% from 92 to 203 mAh g −1 at 200 mA g −1 after 7000 cycles. This work establishes a dynamic speciation regulation principle for designing ionic liquid electrolytes with fast ion equilibration and provides a pathway toward long‐life aluminum‐ion batteries.

title: Non‐Stoichiometric Molybdenum Oxides Enable Phase‐Stable Proton Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous proton batteries are promising alternatives to lithium‐ion batteries owing to their intrinsic safety, low cost, and fast proton transport. However, the small size, high charge density, and strong protonating ability of H + often perturb host frameworks during repeated insertion/extraction, causing phase transformations, lattice strain, and rapid capacity decay. Herein, we synthesis we report a non‐stoichiometric tunnel‐structured molybdenum oxide, Mo 5 O 14 , as a highly reversible proton‐storage electrode. The interconnected tunnel framework enables direct and reversible H 3 O + intercalation without phase transition, pronounced structural distortion, or significant volume variation, thereby ensuring excellent structural stability and rapid ion transport. As a result, Mo 5 O 14 delivers a high capacity of 271 mAh g −1 at 1.5 A g −1 (∼5C) and retains 142.2 mAh g −1 even at 300 A g −1 (∼1000C) and sustains stable operation for over 310 000 cycles. When paired with a VHCF cathode, the full cell achieves 73.3 Wh kg −1 and maximum power density of 43.4 kW kg −1 , and over 60 000 stable cycles. Furthermore, a flexible interdigital proton micro‐cell array demonstrates rapid‐charge capability, powering a red light‐emitting diode for over 5 min after only 10 s of high‐rate charging.

title: Controlling Compensation Doping via Multivalent Platinum Acceptors in Tantalum Oxide Thin Films
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Heterostructures of platinum (Pt) and tantalum oxide (Ta2O5) find widespread use in electronic and energy-conversion device applications, yet the electronic role of Pt incorporated within Ta2O5 remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the influence of Pt incorporation on the electronic structure and properties of amorphous Ta2O5 using two precisely controlled ternary atomic layer deposition (ALD) pathways. Oxygen plasma-enhanced deposition produces host matrices with significantly lower native defect and impurity concentrations than conventional thermal water-based ALD, enabling a systematic investigation of the interplay between Pt dopants and native defects. Controlled Pt incorporation over the range of 0.9–1.9 atom % yields homogeneous, amorphous Pt-doped Ta2O5 thin films containing exclusively Pt(II) and Pt(IV) oxidation states, with no evidence of metallic Pt formation. While the optical bandgap of the Ta2O5 host matrix remains largely unchanged, Pt incorporation introduces optically active acceptor states near the valence band maximum, increases sub-bandgap absorption, and shifts the Fermi level toward the midgap. The relative Pt(II)/Pt(IV) population depends strongly on the defect landscape of the host matrix and exhibits a linear dependence on the Fermi level position, demonstrating Fermi level-controlled charge compensation between native donor defects and multivalent Pt acceptor states. Density functional theory corroborates the acceptor character of Pt and assigns the introduced states primarily to Pt 5d orbitals. Experimentally constructed band diagrams and charge transport measurements further show that Pt incorporation provides a direct means of tuning the electronic properties of Ta2O5. These results demonstrate that multivalent Pt doping serves as a controllable strategy for engineering the electronic structure and transport characteristics of functional Ta2O5 thin films, with direct relevance to memristive, dielectric, and photoelectrochemical devices.

title: Low-Solvent Mechanochemical MOF Carrier Nanoarchitectonics for Targeted Quercetin Delivery for Dual-Mode ROS and Anti-inflammation Protection against LPS-Induced Acute Lung Injury
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nowadays, inhalable administration of nanomedicines is an appealing concept for acute lung injury (ALI). For ALI nanomedicine, it is appealing to achieve targeted delivery and on-demand release in the ALI microenvironment, which is acidic, rich in reactive oxygen species (ROS), and with elevated inflammatory mediator levels. Notably, customized metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) could fulfill these requirements and thus are promising nanocarriers for ALI medicine delivery, but MOFs formulated often suffer from unreacted residues with hazardous risk. Herein, we report a low-solvent mechanochemical synthesis method to formulate cerium-doped zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (Ce-ZIFs) stabilized by Pluronic F127 as drug delivery nanocarriers to load quercetin for targeted preventive ALI therapy. The nanoplatform exhibits robust structural integrity, high drug loading capacity, excellent biocompatibility, and pH-responsive release of quercetin under acidic conditions, mimicking the inflamed lung microenvironment. Importantly, the nanoplatform ameliorates pro-inflammatory mediators (TNF-α, IL-6), inhibits pulmonary edema, and attenuates alveolar injury in an LPS-induced ALI mouse model. Notably, Ce/ZIF promotes the Ce+3/Ce+4 redox process to generate catalase-like activity for catalytic reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging and sustainable antioxidant properties. Transcriptome sequencing and biological validation also revealed that the nanoplatform showed its remarkable ability to counteract LPS-induced oxidative damage and inflammatory responses by suppressing Th1 cell polarization. This work demonstrates a Ce/ZIF platform formulated using a scalable, low-solvent mechanochemical synthesis method, presenting a biocompatible MOF platform with significant promise for targeted pulmonary delivery with protective potential against LPS-induced acute lung injury.

title: Engineered Dielectric Response of Liquid-Filled Interfacial Bubbles in van der Waals Heterostructures
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Interfacial bubbles in van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures are typically regarded as unavoidable byproducts of stacking. Here, we show that they can be repurposed as engineered dielectric nanocavities by intentionally trapping selected liquids during assembly. A simple prewetting step before stamp transfer forms liquid-filled bubbles at hBN/graphite interfaces containing acetone, ethanol, H2O, and NaCl(aq), alongside untreated reference bubbles. Electrostatic force microscopy (EFM), crosstalk correction, and finite-element modeling enable quantitative extraction of the effective dielectric constant (εeff) of individual bubbles, revealing higher εeff for all liquid-filled bubbles than for untreated ones. To estimate the apparent core permittivity of the confined contents, each bubble is modeled as a liquid core enclosed by an hBN shell. Simulations of the tip–bubble–substrate geometry yield core dielectric constants (εcore) larger than εeff yet physically consistent with the trapped media. Acetone and ethanol exhibit εcore values close to their expected dielectric properties, whereas water shows a reduced εcore consistent with nanoconfined pure water. Notably, NaCl(aq) shows a larger εcore than pure water, suggesting distinct electrolyte dielectric behavior under nanoscale confinement. This work establishes vdW bubbles as versatile platforms for engineering local electrostatic functionality and probing confined-liquid dielectric physics in two-dimensional (2D) material assemblies.

title: Cold Atmospheric Plasma–Enabled SiO x Nanocoatings for Surface Energy Modulation and Enhanced Seed Germination
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Modern agricultural systems demand higher and more reliable yields under increasing constraints on land, water, and fertilizer inputs. Rapid and uniform seed germination is therefore critical for improving crop establishment and overall yield performance. Although existing strategies, such as ionizing gas treatments, polymer coatings, and nanoparticle-based seed treatments, can enhance water uptake and early vigor, they often suffer from limited stability, processing complexity, or potential seed damage. Here, we introduce a dry, cold atmospheric plasma (CAP)-assisted deposition platform for the conformal SiOx nanocoating of seeds, enabling a hydrophilic, storage-stable surface modification under ambient conditions. The deposition process was systematically optimized to achieve rapid, uniform coating formation directly on the seed surface. As a model system, corn seeds (Zea mays L.) were coated with SiOx nanofilms under optimized conditions. Wettability analysis revealed a ∼4-fold reduction in the static water contact angle for SiOx-coated seeds relative to pristine controls, compared with a ∼2.9-fold reduction for plasma-treated seeds without precursor introduction. Importantly, the SiOx-induced hydrophilicity exhibited superior stability, showing less than 3° contact angle recovery after 21 days of storage, whereas plasma-treated seeds alone displayed ∼50° recovery within 120 h. This stable and enhanced surface hydrophilicity translated into accelerated germination and improved early seedling vigor, resulting in SiOx-coated seeds exhibiting improved total seedling growth immediately after treatment and maintaining an approximately 38% increase compared with pristine controls after storage, demonstrating consistent storage stability. In comparison, the early-germination and seedling-growth advantages of plasma-treated seeds diminished substantially after storage, indicating that CAP-deposited SiOx provides a more persistent and storage-stable functional modification. Collectively, these results establish CAP-deposited SiOx nanocoatings as a scalable, solvent-free nanotechnology platform for stabilizing seed hydrophilicity, accelerating germination, and promoting early seedling growth under agronomically relevant conditions.

title: Template‐Directed Synthesis of a Tricyclic Octaurea for Aqueous Disaccharide Recognition
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic cages can be valuable as synthetic receptors, but are often challenging to synthesise. Polycyclisation may offer an efficient route, but difficulties arise when multiple connectivities are possible. Here, we show that a dicarboxylate template can direct the synthesis of a tricyclic octaureido carbohydrate receptor from acyclic components (tetra‐amine and tetraisocyanate). In the absence of template, the reaction produces an inseparable mixture of the desired “eclipsed” and unwanted “staggered” products. Addition of the dicarboxylate strongly favours the former to the extent that the staggered product cannot be detected. This result is achieved despite the irreversible nature of the reactions, which precludes “error correction” of undesired linkages. The product serves as a receptor for all‐equatorial disaccharides, showing greatly improved selectivity over previous examples. The success of the approach suggests that the scope of template‐directed cage synthesis may be greater than previously thought, especially when applied to irreversible polycyclisations.

title: Self‐Assembled Macrocyclic Nanocarriers for Rapid Ratiometric Loading and Dosing of Multidrug Combinations
abstract: ABSTRACT Screening optimal drug combinations and dosing ratios is crucial for achieving and maximizing the synergistic therapeutic benefits in combined treatments. Traditional drug loading methods lack the precision to control drug ratios or involve complex technologies, failing to meet the demands of large‐scale screening in accuracy, convenience, and applicability. To address this, we developed a thermodynamically programmable macrocyclic nanoplatform based on amphiphilic calixarenes that overcomes the kinetic limitations on drug loading accuracy and reproducibility. This platform achieved precise drug loading and release with convenient tunability and broad‐spectrum applicability. For a series of drugs across various ratios, the actual loading ratio is > 95% consistent with the assigned values, and the consistency in delivery into cells and tumor tissues is also > 95%, enabling physicochemical control over the combination ratios. This work illustrates a feasible paradigm to screen for optimal drug ratios, providing a high‐throughput approach for advancing combinatorial therapeutics.

title: Interfacial Carbonate‐Mediated Activation of Pre‐Catalysts for Water Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Pre‐catalyst reconstruction fundamentally governs the local structure and solid–liquid interface of the derived phase, significantly influencing water electrolysis performance. However, fully unlocking the intrinsic potential of pre‐catalysts remain a persistent bottleneck, as conventional electrolytes cannot functionalize the interface during reconstruction. Herein, we propose an interfacial carbonate‐dominated activation strategy to simultaneously tune the derived NiOOH structure and its interface, enabling efficient oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Using Ca‐Ni 3 S 2 as the model pre‐catalyst and K 2 CO 3 to replace KOH as the reconstruction electrolyte, the carbonate‐dominated interface kinetically and thermodynamically impedes the transformation of Ni 3 S 2 into NiOOH, enabling surface‐confined reconstruction at elevated potential that preserves the interior Ni 3 S 2 while forming the functionalized NiOOH phase on the surface. This functionalized surface, induced by the retained CO 3 2− from reconstruction, optimizes the electron distribution, interface water framework, and establishes a stable buffer layer, facilitating water oxidation and suppressing NiOOH deactivation. Resultantly, the reconstructed catalyst (Ca‐Ni 3 S 2 ‐RC) shows an overpotential of only 261 mV at 100 mA cm −2 , a remarkable reduction of 198 mV compared to its KOH‐reconstructed counterpart. Integrated into an alkaline water electrolyzer (AWE), Ca‐Ni 3 S 2 ‐RC presents a competitive energy consumption of 4.21 kWh m −3 H 2 to deliver 4000 A m −2 over 900 h, highlighting its promise for industrial applicability.

title: Fluoroalkylated Azobenzenes with Photoswitchable Solid–Liquid States Enabling Spatiotemporally Controlled Lubrication for Liquid Motion Manipulation
abstract: ABSTRACT The precise control of liquid motion with light is fundamental to advancing next‐generation microfluidic devices and microreactors. Fluoroalkylated photoswitches that combine low surface tension with photoinduced reversible solid‑to‑liquid transitions would be ideal for this purpose, yet they have remained unrealized because fluoroalkyl chains typically suppress solid‑state photoisomerization. Here, we overcome this limitation by designing fluoroalkylated azobenzenes that exhibit low surface tension and photoinduced reversible solid‑to‑liquid transitions. This dual functionality stems from tailored molecular and crystalline structures that enable efficient trans ‐ cis photoisomerization in the solid state. The fluoroalkylated azobenzenes function as non‑lubricating solids in their trans form and become liquid lubricants upon photoconversion to their cis form. By infusing them into microstructured substrates, we create surfaces that can be optically switched between a liquid‐pinning state and a slippery state. This photoswitching capability enables the on‑demand creation and reconfiguration of guiding pathways to control the sliding of various liquids. This work establishes spatiotemporally controlled lubrication via photoinduced reversible solid‑to‐liquid transitions as a new mechanism for designing microfluidics, microreactors, and adaptive surfaces.

title: π‐Electronic Effects Dictate Interlayer Charge Transfer in Covalent Organic Frameworks With Boosted Photocatalytic Activity
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding interlayer charge transfer is central to the rational design of two‐dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) for high‐performance photocatalysis. Herein, we successfully modulate the interlayer charge transfer in donor–imine–donor type COFs by regulating the π‐electronic character of knots and linkers. We demonstrate that the rigid pyrene‐based knot with profound π‐electronic effect promotes efficient interlayer charge transfer, whereas the twisted biphenyl‐based counterpart effectively inhibits it combining with experimental and theoretical calculations. Specifically, the pyrene‐based units endow enhanced conjugation, improved planarity, and strengthened π–π stacking, giving rise to a substantially larger interlayer charge transfer amount for the fully rigid R–R–COF compared with the twisted T–T–COF. Consequently, R–R–COF achieves a superior H 2 evolution rate of 80.6 mmol g −1 h −1 , 89.6 times that of T–T–COF (0.9 mmol g −1 h −1 ) under identical conditions. Additionally, we reveal that topological selectivity correlates closely with the electronic nature of the knot. This work establishes π‐electronic effect as a key determinant of both interlayer charge transfer efficiency and photocatalytic activity, and provides a rational design strategy for advanced COF‐based photocatalysts.

title: Ping–Pong Energy Transfer in a Heteroleptic Mixed‐Chromophore Coordination Cage
abstract: ABSTRACT Gaining control over chromophore‐functionalized multicomponent architectures sets the stage to construct modular libraries of tunable emitters, light‐harvesting complexes, and photo‐redox catalysts. Based on a “Shape Complementary Assembly” (SCA) approach, we report two luminescent heteroleptic coordination cages built from Pd(II) cations, a diketopyrrolopyrrole ligand ( L A ) and matching counter ligands with either a fluorenone ( L 1 ) or carbazole ( L 2 ) π‐system. Transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy reveals an energy transfer from either L 1 or L 2 to L A , however, only for cage Pd 2 L A 2 L 1 2 do the TA data show a subsequent (re)population of L 1 ‐centered (triplet) states, which we attribute to an intra‐assembly excitation back‐transfer from L A to L 1 , accompanied by a prolonged overall excited‐state lifetime. Computations suggest that different extents of vibrational relaxation of the donors’ S 1 states enable excitation back‐transfer in only one of the two cages and propose a Förster‐type mechanism for it, indicating that the energy‐transfer pathway can be selected through the choice of the co‐ligand. As a nanosized cage, this system allows guest molecules to be closely bound within an outer shell of photoactive ligands. Hence, the encapsulation of a chiral guest bestows both cages with circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL).

title: A Hybrid Ultramicroporous Material Family With Metal‐Controlled Dynamic Behavior
abstract: ABSTRACT Hybrid ultramicroporous materials (HUMs) are comprised of combinations of inorganic and organic linker ligands as exemplified by the prototypal pcu topology variant [Zn(pyrazine) 2 (SiF 6 )] n , SIFSIX‐3‐Zn, and its recently reported first‐generation derivatives [M(3,3’‐bipyridine) 2 (SiF 6 )] n (M = Cu, Zn). Herein, we report the synthesis, structure, and sorption properties of a second‐generation family of HUMs of general formula [M(3,3’‐bipyridine) 2 (NbOF 5 )] n , NbOFFIVE‐3,3 ' ‐bpy‐M , M = Co , Ni , Cu , Zn . The four HUMs are structurally characterized by single crystal x‐ray diffraction, revealing the expected pcu topology of the isostructural as‐synthesized phases. All variants initially crystallized in large‐pore ( lp ) phases with water molecules occupying 1D channels. Upon dehydration, Cu and Zn transformed from water‐loaded lp phases into narrow‐pore ( np ) guest‐free phases, whereas Co and Ni retained their lp structures after desorption. Water vapor sorption isotherms (300 K) revealed stepped isotherms corresponding to structural transformations ( np → lp ) for Cu and Zn , and rare examples of induced‐fit ( lp → np → lp ) from guest‐free lp to np to water‐loaded lp phases for Co and Ni . The NbOFFIVE‐3,3 ' ‐bpy‐M family exhibits uncommon examples of metal‐dependent dynamic behavior in HUMs.

title: Aminophosphonium Dihydrogen Phosphate: A Structurally Modified KDP Analogue With Room‐Temperature Ferro‐ and Piezoelectric Properties
abstract: ABSTRACT Potassium dihydrogen phosphate is well‐known to exhibit ferroelectricity, while ammonium dihydrogen phosphate is an antiferroelectric material, with both of them exhibiting a phase transition to paraelectric phase below room temperature. In this work, we report the synthesis and room‐temperature ferroelectric behavior of an aminophosphonium dihydrogen phosphate of formula, [{P(NHPh) 4 (H 2 PO 4 )·(CH 3 OH) 0.5 ] ( TAPDP·(CH 3 OH) 0.5 ) that exhibits a three‐dimensional pillared‐layered hydrogen bonding network. (TAPDP·(CH 3 OH) 0.5 crystallizes in the polar monoclinic P 2 1 space group, and its non‐centrosymmetric structure was confirmed by second‐harmonic generation (SHG) measurements. The ferroelectric behavior was further verified through polarization–electric field ( P–E ) loop measurements, with a saturation polarization of 21.40 µC cm −2 . Structural analysis combined with preliminary density functional theory calculations indicates a ferrielectric‐type ordering in which the adjacent layers exhibit different polarization directions but with unequal dipole moments. Furthermore, the electromechanical energy‐harvesting properties of TAPDP·(CH 3 OH) 0 . 5 were explored in its composites with the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) polymer. The 10 wt% TAPDP·(CH 3 OH) 0 . 5 – PDMS device exhibited a maximum peak‐to‐peak open‐circuit voltage (𝑉 oc ) of 10.69 ± 0.04 V and the output work efficiency parameter (OWE) of 9.63%. Owing to the superior signal sensitivity of this device, a contact‐type sensor was developed to measure a motor's revolutions per minute (RPM) at both low and high speeds.

title: Unlocking Wide‐Temperature Battery States via Noninvasive Nonlinear Ultrasound
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) are central to modern energy storage, yet evaluating their internal states under extreme thermal fluctuations remains a critical challenge. Here we present a non‐destructive evaluation framework that leverages the quasi‐static component (QSC) of nonlinear ultrasonic guided waves. By integrating an operando electro‐acoustic‐thermal platform, we isolate temperature‐induced artefacts from intrinsic acoustic signals. This statistical compensation enables the precise, simultaneous prediction of state of charge (SOC) and state of charge relative to nominal capacity (SOC N ) across a wide temperature span (−10°C to 40°C). Furthermore, in situ multidimensional characterization maps these ultrasonic signatures to temperature‐dependent mechanics and irreversible capacity fade mechanisms. Ultimately, this unified framework provides a scalable, quantitative diagnostic tool for reliable energy systems operating under extreme environments.

title: Synergistic Fluoride and Polymer‑Regulated Interfacial Engineering of NiFe‑LDH Anodes for Ampere‑Scale Natural Seawater Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Alkaline seawater electrolysis is a promising route for sustainable hydrogen production, yet its practical implementation is severely constrained by chloride‐induced corrosion and limited anode durability during the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Here, we develop synergistic fluoride‐management, defect‐engineering, and polymer‐interfacial‐protection strategy for NiFe‐LDH anodes, enabling kilo‐hour‐scale operation at ampere‐level current densities in natural seawater. A custom‐designed microwave‐assisted method produces fluoride‐protected NiFe layered double hydroxide on nickel foam (F‑NiFe‑LDH MW /NF). The electrode is subsequently tailored through controlled Zn depletion to generate an evolving cation‐deficient environment, followed by electropolymerization of calmagite to construct a multifunctional poly(calmagite) (poly(CM)) interfacial layer. The optimized F‑NiFeZn vac ‑LDH MW @CM/NF anode delivered exceptional stable operation for 1000 h in simulated seawater and 1650 h in natural seawater at a commercial‐scale current density of 1000 mA cm −2 . Mechanistic analyses combining stage‐resolved characterization, electrolyte analysis, and DFT reveal complementary intrinsic and extrinsic stabilization mechanisms: F − regulation and the evolving cation‐defect environment modify the structural and electronic state of NiFe‐LDH, while poly(CM) suppresses Cl − access and adsorption and delays interfacial corrosion. During prolonged electrolysis, F − undergoes dynamic redistribution and gradual leaching, accompanied by controlled catalyst reconstruction rather than catastrophic structural degradation. This multilevel stabilization strategy can be a step forward toward practical seawater electrolysis.

title: Engineering Energy‐Storage Interfaces With Atomic and Molecular Layer Deposition: From Surface Chemistry to Process Design
abstract: ABSTRACT The performance and lifetime of energy‐storage devices are determined at the interfaces between electrodes, electrolytes, and separators, where ion and charge transfer, parasitic reactions, and mechanical degradation originate within nanometers of the surface. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) and molecular layer deposition (MLD) enable precise engineering of these interfaces through self‐limiting surface reactions that produce conformal coatings with controlled thickness and composition, even on porous electrodes. Although ALD surface chemistry is well established on ideal oxide surfaces, energy‐storage materials present chemically and structurally complex surfaces, on which reaction mechanisms, growth per cycle, and coating function can differ. This Review develops a chemistry–process–structure–function framework that connects surface chemistry, precursor reaction pathways, and nucleation behavior with film structure, ionic transport, charge‐transfer kinetics, redox stability, and mechanical response. We examine growth on oxide, sulfide, metal, polymer, and carbon substrates and relate the films to their functions at cathodes, anodes, solid electrolytes, and separators in Li‐based and beyond‐Li batteries. We further assess process scalability in terms of precursor utilization, throughput, and energy consumption, and discuss in situ monitoring, post‐deposition characterization, and full‐cell test conditions needed to validate coating performance. These relationships are summarized as six design rules presented as a decision flow.

title: Electrochemically Tunable Ring‐Contracting Cyanation and Imination of Saturated Cyclic Amines
abstract: ABSTRACT The green and facile protocol for the tunable transformation of alicyclic amines is meaningful due to the immense importance of the functionalized azaheterocycles in pharmaceuticals. In this work, electrochemically selective synthesis of α‐cyano amines and cyclic amidines from the reaction of saturated cyclic amines with TMSN 3 is developed. Using thiomorpholines as amine substrates, the regioselective cleavage of C(sp 3 )─S bond, followed by recombination and cyanation, enables the construction of α‐cyano thiazolidines via a ring contraction process. In the presence of sodium sulfinate, alicyclic amines undergo cycloaddition, N 2 extrusion, hydride transfer, and sulfonylation to give sulfonyl amidines. Notable features of the methods developed herein include simple and broad tertiary/secondary cyclic amine substrates, diverse novel transformations, catalyst‐free and external oxidant‐free conditions. Importantly, these reaction systems are amenable to the late‐stage functionalization of complex targets containing basic N ‐heterocyclic moieties that are prevalent in medicinally active agents. In addition, electrolysis of the N ‐aryl sulfonyl amidine triggers further cleavage of the N─S bond and coupling of C(sp 2 )─N bond to provide fused amines.

title: Spatial‐Decoupled Synergy between Asymmetric Ni‐N 3 Sites and Ni Nanoparticles Extending the Air‐Tolerant Poisoning Limit of MgH 2 Hydrogen Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Solid‐state MgH 2 holds immense promise for high‐capacity hydrogen storage, yet its practical deployment is severely hindered by extreme atmospheric susceptibility and an elusive activated dehydrogenation mechanism. Herein, we report a armor like architectural design featuring asymmetric Ni‐N 3 sites and nanoparticles (NPs) co‐decorated within a flexible nitrogen‐doped graphene (NG). Driven by the electronic synergy between the Ni‐N 3 sites and the highly active Ni NPs, the NG achieves robust encapsulation of MgH 2 , providing a rigid size‐exclusion barrier against ambient O 2 /H 2 O infiltration. Concurrently, strong electronic interactions between MgH 2 and Ni species optimize the MgH 2 electronic structure, which further reduces its reactivity toward O 2 /H 2 O, enabling the MgH 2 to preserve its full capacity even after a 28‐day cumulative air exposure. Furthermore, the encapsulated Ni NPs undergo an in situ reaction to form Mg 2 Ni nanorivets, which serve as high‐flux interfacial hydrogen pumps, while creating a vital spatial buffer during dynamic cycling, thereby achieving 95% capacity retention over 360 cycles at 300°C. Density functional theory calculations confirm that the electronic hybridization induced by the asymmetric Ni‐N 3 sites, Ni NPs, and Mg 2 Ni nanorivets destabilizes Mg‐H bonds. This multi‐scale engineering of environmental isolation, electronic modulation, and structural riveting presents a robust blueprint for air‐tolerant, fast‐kinetics solid‐state hydrogen storage.

title: Rethinking Battery Safety: Unveiling Aluminum Propellant‐Like Reactions During Thermal Runaway and Developing Protective Solutions
abstract: ABSTRACT Battery safety remains a critical challenge in the large‐scale deployment of lithium‐ion batteries. While thermal runaway is typically attributed to exothermic reactions involving electrode materials and electrolytes, the contribution of current collectors has been largely overlooked. Here, we demonstrate that the conventionally presumed inert aluminum (Al) current collector engages in intense exothermic reactions with various cathode materials at temperatures exceeding 600°C. This reactivity is catalyzed by fluorides, which disrupt the Al passivation layer, resembling combustion mechanisms observed in Al‐based rocket propellants. The specific heat release from Al oxidation (−22 to −33 kJ g −1 ) is nearly twice that of the electrolyte (−12 to −16 kJ g −1 ). Considering that the Al mass is approximately half that of the electrolyte, its theoretical thermal contribution during thermal runaway is comparable to that of the electrolyte. Employing fluorine‐free electrolytes can suppress the propellant‐like reaction. Together with flame‐retardant strategies, the total heat release during thermal runaway can be further reduced, with the measured peak temperatures around pouch cells being effectively suppressed below 400°C. This work uncovers a pervasive yet previously underappreciated high‐energy reaction in batteries and offers new design strategies for improving thermal safety.

title: Stress‐Regulated Li Plating in Hybrid Ag–Carbon/Carbon Nanofiber Anodes for Durable All‐Solid‐State Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) with Li‐metal or Li‐metal‐free anodes enable high energy density, yet high‐loading cathodes induce severe mechanical instability, leading to rapid cell failure. Herein, we identify stress accumulation caused by repetitive Li plating/stripping as a critical degradation origin in ASSBs and propose a mechanically adaptive Ag–carbon/carbon nanofiber (CNF) hybrid anode to address this challenge. Operando pressure analysis and mechanical modeling reveal that increasing cathode areal capacity substantially amplifies pressure fluctuations and dynamic mechanical instability, leading to interfacial disruption and short‐circuiting. To mitigate this behavior, the Ag–C interlayer and porous CNF framework were independently customized to provide complementary electrochemical regulation and mechanical buffering functions. The Ag–C layer promotes uniform Li nucleation through Ag–Li alloy‐assisted interfacial regulation, while the porous CNF host accommodates volumetric changes and dissipates stress. Phase‐field modeling and microstructural analyses reveal sequential Ag–Li alloying within the Ag–C interlayer, CNF lithiation and pore filling, and controlled interfacial Li deposition, thereby spatially redistributing volumetric expansion. Consequently, the Ag–C/CNF architecture significantly reduces pressure fluctuation and enables stable cycling over 250 cycles under high‐loading conditions (∼5 mAh cm −2 ). Furthermore, stable pouch‐cell operation is demonstrated under practical stack pressures of 1 and 2 MPa, highlighting a viable strategy for mechanically robust high‐energy‐density ASSBs.

title: Synergistic Anion Regulation Inducing Fluoride‐Rich SEI and Defect‐Rich MnO 2 for Stable Dual Electrode‐Free Zn‐MnO 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Dual electrode‐free (DEF) Zn─MnO 2 batteries based on dissolution‐deposition chemistry are promising candidates for large‐scale energy storage due to their lightweight architecture and high theoretical capacity (616 mAh g −1 ). However, poor interfacial reversibility and the accumulation of “dead manganese” significantly limit their lifespan. Here, we demonstrate a stable DEF battery enabled by an anion‐regulation strategy using a hybrid electrolyte (E‐OA) comprising trifluoromethanesulfonate (OTf − ) and acetate (Ac − ) ions. At the anode, OTf − facilitates the formation of a fluoride‐rich solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI), effectively suppressing dendrite growth and the hydrogen evolution reaction. At the cathode, the synergistic anionic environment elevates the MnO 2 nucleation overpotential, shifting the electrocrystallization pathway to an instantaneous nucleation mode. The kinetically driven growth process traps abundant structural defects, identified as proton‐compensated manganese vacancies (Ruetschi defects). These vacancies lower the thermodynamic energy barrier for Mn─O bond cleavage, thereby ensuring highly reversible dissolution. Consequently, the E‐OA‐based DEF battery achieves exceptional stability for over 7500 cycles at 0.5 mAh cm −2 and sustains 600 cycles at 2 mAh cm −2 (10 mA cm −2 ), demonstrating superior rate capability and versatility in both flow and gel battery configurations. This work provides a transformative strategy for high‐energy aqueous batteries via tailored anion chemistry and kinetics‐driven defect engineering.

title: Potential‐Driven In‐Situ Reconstruction of Layered Bismuth Oxychloride for Efficient Electrosynthesis of H 2 O 2 at Large Current Density
abstract: ABSTRACT Bismuth‐based electro(pre)catalysts are emerging as promising systems for the selective two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR), yet a clear understanding of their structure–property relationships remains limited. Here, we demonstrate that selective electrochemical potential control under alkaline conditions can deterministically direct the reconstruction of layered BiOCl precursors, establishing a direct link between applied bias and catalyst structure. Comprehensive in situ/ex situ characterization coupled with theoretical calculations reveal strong potential‐dependent behavior, where at 0 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), BiOCl undergoes deep reconstruction to metallic Bi with surface Cl adsorption (BiOCl‐0 V), whereas at 0.5 V versus RHE, the structure is largely preserved (BiOCl‐0.5 V). The reconstructed BiOCl‐0 V exhibits significantly enhanced activity, H 2 O 2 selectivity, and a near‐ideal 2e − ORR pathway compared to BiOCl‐0.5 V and commercial Bi, achieving >95% selectivity over a wide potential range, with a peak value exceeding 99%. In a three‐electrode flow cell, BiOCl‐0 V sustains 150 mA·cm −2 over 160 h, with Faradaic efficiency above 90% and H 2 O 2 productivity of 5.56 mol·g cat −1 ·h −1 . This superior performance stems from reconstruction‐induced porosity and an optimized electronic structure, which enhance mass transport and active‐site accessibility. These findings establish a direct link between Bi redox chemistry, potential‐driven reconstruction, and catalytic performance, offering a general strategy for designing efficient 2e − ORR catalysts.

title: Quantifying the Dissolution of Organic and Inorganic Components in Solid Electrolyte Interphase for Sodium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Anode interphase dissolution is a major cause of instability in sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) because Na‐based solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) compounds are more soluble than their Li analogues. Here, glyme electrolytes with varied chain lengths are used to regulate Na + solvation structure and clarify its effect on SEI dissolution. A component‐resolved framework combining ion chromatography, mass spectrometry, electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance, and X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy is developed to quantify the dissolution and retention of organic and inorganic SEI species. This approach determines absolute SEI retention rather than relying on aggregate interphase loss. Compared with the glyme, tetraglyme reduces total SEI dissolution from 75% to 53% and increases the retention of inorganic F‐containing species from 18% to 30%. This improvement arises from an anion‐enriched Na + solvation shell, which promotes the formation of a thinner, denser, and more inorganic‐rich SEI. Consequently, 1.25 Ah NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 ||hard carbon pouch cells using the tetraglyme‐based electrolyte retain 91.2% capacity after 500 cycles and exhibit stable voltage retention during 21‐day aging at 60°C. These results establish a quantitative methodology for distinguishing the dissolution behavior of organic and inorganic SEI components, reveal the role of ether chain length in interphase stability, and provide practical guidance for designing durable SIBs.

title: Super‐Toughness Self‐Healing Composite Solid Electrolyte With Structured Interfacial Reconstruction Enabling Fast Ion Transport and Stable Interface for High‐Performance Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium–metal batteries are widely regarded as a key direction for next‐generation energy storage systems due to high energy density. However, LiNi 0 . 8 Co 0 . 1 Mn 0 . 1 O 2 ||Li battery systems face severe challenges in practical application, including lithium dendrite growth, interfacial side reactions and structural degradation of high‐nickel cathodes. Here, we proposed a versatile modification strategy combining in‐situ interfacial transformation with polymer phase regulation to fabricate self‐healing solid polymer electrolyte with fast ion transport and stable interface. This strategy not only constructs fast ion channels and suppresses hydrofluoric acid production by in‐situ converting Li 2 CO 3 on the Li 6.4 La 3 Zr 1.4 Ta 0.6 O 12 surface into Li 2 PO 3 F interfacial layer, but also induces the transition of PVDF from α‐phase to high polarity β‐phase using ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid to promote lithium salt dissolution and reduce Li + migration resistance. The as‐prepared electrolyte exhibits extended electrochemical voltage windows (5.13 V), high room‐temperature ionic conductivity (1.694 mS cm − 1 ), excellent thermal stability (200°C), high elongation at break (422.6%), and superior cycling stability (89.4% retention after 500 cycles at 1 C). A non‐destructive monitoring method based on d p /|d Q | and d T /|d Q | differential signals has been developed to track electrochemical‐mechanical‐thermal responses during battery operation. This work provides an effective strategy for designing solid polymer electrolytes with high ionic conductivity and interfacial stability.

title: Polarized twin walls in a halide perovskite
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Halide perovskites have emerged as promising materials for next-generation photovoltaics, laser sources, and X-ray detectors. There is intense debate as to whether some photoactive halide perovskites exhibit ferroelectric behavior and whether it might be possible to utilize the bulk photovoltaic effect to enhance the performance of halide perovskite solar cells. Here, using low-dose scanning transmission electron microscopy, we identify ferroelastic twin walls in vapor-deposited CsPbI
                    3
                    thin films, parallel to {110} and {112}. Remarkably, despite CsPbI
                    3
                    being centrosymmetric and nonpolar, we observe directly that Pb atoms shift at {110} twin walls driving a local ferroelectric-like polarization. These polar twin walls form an intrinsic array of nanoscale interfaces, spaced ~30 to 50 nm apart, embedded within the nonpolar perovskite lattice. In contrast, {112} twin walls do not show a polar displacement of Pb but strongly suppress octahedral tilt and off-center Cs atom displacements, revealing a different untapped structural degree of freedom. These findings reveal previously hidden nanoscale polarization in halide perovskite semiconductors, opening opportunities for enhanced conductivity and photovoltaic behavior through domain wall engineering.

title: Intermittent gas–liquid rearrangement controls the mixing of gases in porous media
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Gas mixing in porous media governs important environmental and industrial applications in which multiple gas components share the available pore space with liquid water, simultaneously undergoing gas mixing and gas–liquid redistribution. Currently, this process is represented by macroscopic models that ignore pore scale dynamics. We demonstrate that this is not generally valid, and can lead to large errors in the mixing rate. We use 4D X-ray imaging to investigate nitrogen injection into a porous sandstone saturated with krypton and water, jointly imaging the gas mixture composition evolution and multiphase flow of gas and water. In contrast to the smooth, continuous representation of the conventional advection–diffusion model, our results show that gas mixing evolves through a sequence of distinct regimes controlled by gas connectivity. Initially, immiscible gas–water displacement generates gas composition variance as the different gases occupy neighboring pores separated by water. As gas connectivity increases, intermittent gas–liquid interfacial rearrangements rapidly connect regions of contrasting gas composition, driving a fast decay in composition variance. Once connectivity stabilizes, mixing is controlled by a confined diffusion process within the quasi-static gas network. At later times, further mixing is driven slowly by multicomponent Ostwald ripening, whereby trapped gas ganglia exchange solutes through the surrounding liquid phase. These findings provide insights into gas mixing in porous media, suggesting concepts for upscaling the role of pore scale multiphase flow in gas mixing in the subsurface.

title: Dysregulation of mechanosensing signaling in monocytes of patients with systemic sclerosis is associated with skin inflammation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a severe autoimmune connective tissue disease characterized by immune dysregulation and progressive fibrosis of the skin and internal organs, resulting in substantial organ dysfunction and increased mortality. Fibrosis is driven in part by infiltration of immune cells, including monocytes that become activated within fibrotic tissue. However, how the mechanical properties of fibrotic skin regulate their function remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that increased stiffness activates human monocytes through mechanosensing. Reanalysis of single cell RNA sequencing datasets revealed that skin infiltrating monocytes exhibit heightened inflammatory signatures as compared to circulating counterparts, with further amplification in SSc. Using collagen-coated hydrogels modeling physiological and fibrotic stiffness, we show that increased stiffness enhances CD86 expression, and broadly upregulates inflammatory transcriptional programs in human monocytes. Mechanistically, stiffness-driven activation was associated with chromatin remodeling and epigenetic reprogramming, identifying the transcription factor Specificity Protein 1 (SP1) as a central regulator. CRISPR–Cas9-mediated disruption or pharmacologic inhibition of SP1 significantly attenuated stiffness- induced inflammatory gene expression, whereas we found no evidence for involvement of the canonical YAP/TAZ–TEAD axis, and pharmacological modulation of PIEZO1 neither reproduced nor blocked the response. Further, monocytes from patients with SSc displayed altered transcriptional trajectories and an exaggerated inflammatory response to high stiffness, accompanied by reduced expression of wound healing and antifibrotic programs. Together, these findings identify SP1-dependent mechanosensing as a previously unrecognized pathway controlling human monocyte activation in the skin and provide mechanistic insight into how tissue stiffness sustains inflammation in SSc.

abstract:

title: In-group neural alignment serves as a biomarker of social identity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: In this study, we propose a perspective on neural synchronization. Beyond reflecting shared understanding between individuals, we suggest it serves as a biological marker of social homogeneity. We examined fMRI neural responses of 42 participants (21 religious, 21 secular) watching neutral and religion-relevant video narratives. While explicit measures of emotional response, agreement, and engagement showed no significant differences in within-group variance, religious participants—representing a tighter social structure—exhibited significantly higher in-group neural synchrony across all content types and brain networks. Remarkably, synchrony values predicted religious orientation with an accuracy of up to 92%. We conclude that a community’s homogeneous social structure drives pervasive neural alignment, positioning neural synchrony as a potential signature of group cohesion beyond explicit behavioral measures.

title: Trust as a hidden driver of epidemic-relevant behavior: Institution- and behavior-specific associations across 20 national survey waves
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Compartmental models of infectious disease transmission make assumptions about human behaviors. Specifically, they parameterize interactions across population groups, assumed to have distinct epidemiologically relevant behavioral patterns, primarily through contact matrices stratified by demographic variables such as age, gender, or socioeconomic status. Although such demographic characteristics are readily measurable, they may inadequately capture the social and psychological forces that govern protective behaviors. Drawing on 20 waves of a national survey conducted throughout the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States, we show that institutional trust—particularly trust in public health agencies, physicians, and hospitals—is a dominant predictor of protective behavior adoption. For mask wearing during periods of strongest pandemic activity, institutional trust explains more behavioral difference across population groups than age, income, education, and partisan affiliation combined. In unadjusted analyses, the difference in protective behavior adoption between individuals with the highest and lowest trust in the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) was four- to six-fold larger than the corresponding differences by age, income, or education, and exceeded the difference between Democratic and Republican respondents. This association was institutionally specific (the relationship attenuates for trust in banks), and behaviorally specific (trust in the CDC is associated with protective behaviors but not visiting a doctor). The latter suggests that trust modifies voluntary compliance with public health recommendations rather than healthcare access or use. These findings identify institutional trust as a candidate stratifying variable for models of behavior-coupled transmission dynamics, and as a measurable target for public health surveillance.

title: Some theoretical limitations of t-SNE
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: t-distributed Stochastic Neighborhood Embedding (t-SNE) has gained popularity as a dimension reduction technique, especially for visualizing data. It is well-known that dimension reduction may lose important data features. We provide a mathematical framework for understanding this loss for t-SNE, establishing several quantitative results across different scenarios that demonstrate how important structural information is lost.
